_cl_disconnectreason.desc: This cvar contains the reason for the last disconnection, so that mod menus can know why things failed.

_cl_voip_capturedevice_opts.desc: The possible audio capture devices, in \"value\" \"description\" pairs, for gamecode to read.

_pext_infoblobs.desc: RENAME ME WHEN STABLE. Enables the use of very large infokeys containing potentially invalid chars. Note that the userinfo is still limited by sv_userinfo_bytelimit and sv_userinfo_keylimit.

_pext_lerptime.desc: RENAME ME WHEN STABLE. Sends timing hints for interpolation.

_pext_vrinputs.desc: RENAME ME WHEN STABLE. Networks player inputs slightly differently, allowing for greater capabilities, particuarly vr controller info.

_q3bsp_bihtraces.desc: Uses runtime-generated bih collision culling for faster traces.

_s_device_opts.desc: The possible audio output devices, in \"value\" \"description\" pairs, for gamecode to read.

_vid_renderer_opts.desc: The possible video renderer apis, in \"value\" \"description\" pairs, for gamecode to read.

allow_download.desc: If 1, permits downloading. Set to 0 to unconditionally block *ALL* downloads from this server. You may wish to set sv_dlURL if you wish clients to still be able to download content.

allow_download_configs.desc: 1 allows downloading of config files, either with the extension .cfg or in the subdir configs/.\nTHIS IS DANGEROUS AS IT CAN ALLOW PEOPLE TO READ YOUR RCON PASSWORD ETC.

allow_download_copyrighted.desc: 0 blocks download of packages that are considered copyrighted. Specifically, this means packages with a leading 'pak' prefix on the filename.\nIf you take your copyrights seriously, you should also set allow_download_pakmaps 0 and allow_download_pakcontents 0.

allow_download_demos.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the demos/ directory

allow_download_locs.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the locs/ directory

allow_download_logs.desc: 1 permits downloading files with the extension .log\nTHIS IS DANGEROUS AS IT POTENTIALLY ALLOWS PEOPLE TO SEE PASSWORDS OR OTHER PRIVATE INFORMATION.\nNote that it can be switch on/off via rcon.

allow_download_maps.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the maps/ directory

allow_download_models.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the progs/ or models/ directory

allow_download_other.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file that was not covered by any of the directory download blocks.

allow_download_packages.desc: if 1, permits downloading files (from root directory or elsewhere) with known package extensions (eg: pak+pk3). Packages with a name starting 'pak' are covered by allow_download_copyrighted as well.

allow_download_pakcontents.desc: 0: clients may not download non-map files within the server's packages.\n1: clients may download such files so long as the package is not deemed copyrighted, for compat with old clients that do not support package downloads.\n2: client may download such files regardless of copyright state (WARNING! ONLY for consistency with vanilla QuakeWorld!).

allow_download_pakmaps.desc: 0: clients may not download map files within the server's packages.\n1: clients may download such files so long as the package is not deemed copyrighted, for compat with old clients that do not support package downloads.\n2: client may download such files regardless of copyright state (WARNING! Should never be used!).

allow_download_particles.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the particles/ directory

allow_download_refpackages.desc: If set to 1, packages that contain files needed during spawn functions will be become 'referenced' and automatically downloaded to clients.\nThis cvar should probably not be set if you have large packages that provide replacement pickup models on public servers.\nThe path command will show a '(ref)' tag next to packages which clients will automatically attempt to download.

allow_download_root.desc: If set, enables downloading from the root of the gamedir (not the basedir). This setting has a lower priority than extension-based checks.

allow_download_skins.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the skins/ directory

allow_download_sounds.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the sound/ directory

allow_download_textures.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the textures/ directory

allow_download_wads.desc: 0 blocks downloading of any file in the wads/ directory, or is in the root directory with the extension .wad

allow_skybox.desc: This setting says whether clients should skip writing skybox depth when rendering skyboxes/skydomes. Skipping depth writes is required for halflife, quake2, and quake3 compat, but q1 content generally requires depth masking. Empty uses format-specific defaults.

baseskin.desc: The name of the player skin to use as a fallback.

brightness.desc: Brightness is how much 'white' to add to each and every pixel on the screen.

capturecodec.desc: the compression/encoding codec to use.\nWith raw capturing, this should be one of tga,png,jpg,pcx (ie: screenshot extensions).

capturedemoheight.desc: When using capturedemo, this specifies the height of the FBO image used.

capturedemowidth.desc: When using capturedemo, this specifies the width of the FBO image used. Can be larger than your physical monitor.

capturedriver.desc: The driver to use to capture the demo. Use the capture command with no arguments for a list of drivers.

capturerate.desc: The framerate of the video to capture

capturesound.desc: Enables the capturing of game voice. If not using capturedemo, this can be combined with cl_voip_test to capture your own voice.

capturethrottlesize.desc: If set, capturing will slow down significantly if there is less disk space available than this cvar (in mb). This is useful when recording a stream to (ram)disk while another program is simultaneously consuming frames.

cfg_save_aliases.desc: If 1, saves aliases to configs. Note that aliases sent from servers are assumed to be server-specific and are never saved (and are forgotten on map changes, too).

cfg_save_all.desc: If 1, cfg_save ALWAYS saves all cvars. If 0, cfg_save only ever saves archived cvars. If empty, cfg_save saves all cvars only when an explicit filename was given (ie: when not used internally via quit menu options).

cfg_save_auto.desc: If 1, the config will automatically be saved and without prompts. If 0, you'll have to save your config manually (possibly via prompts from the quit menu).

cfg_save_binds.desc: If 1, saves all key bindings to configs.

cfg_save_buttons.desc: If 1, saves the state of things such as +mlook or +forward to configs.

cfg_save_infos.desc: If 1, saves userinfo and serverinfo to configs.

cfg_save_name.desc: This is the config name that is saved by default when no argument is specified.

cl_aliasoverlap.desc: Rename new aliases if they would override cvar names.

cl_autotrack.desc: Specifies the default tracking mode at the start of the map. Use the 'autotrack' command to reset/apply an auto-tracking mode without changing the default.\nValid values are: high, ^hkiller^h, mod, user. Other values are treated as weighting scripts for mvd playback, where available.

cl_autotrack_team.desc: Specifies a team name that should be auto-tracked (players on other teams will not be candidates for autotracking). Accepts * and ? wildcards for awkward chars.

cl_backspeed.desc: The base speed that you move backwards at. If empty, uses the value of cl_forwardspeed instead.

cl_beam_alpha.desc: Specifies the translucency of the lightning beam segments.

cl_beam_trace.desc: Clips the length of any beams according to any walls they may have impacted.

cl_bob.desc: Controls how much the camera position should bob up down as the player runs around.

cl_bobmodel.desc: Controls whether the viewmodel should bob up and down as the player runs around.

cl_c2sImpulseBackup.desc: Prevents the cl_c2spps setting from dropping redundant packets that contain impulses, in an attempt to keep impulses more reliable.

cl_c2sMaxRedundancy.desc: This is the maximum number of input frames to send in each input packet. Values greater than 1 provide redundancy and avoid prediction misses, though you might find cl_c2sdupe provides equivelent result and at lower latency. It is locked at 3 for vanilla quakeworld, and locked at 1 for vanilla netquake.

cl_c2sdupe.desc: Send duplicate copies of packets to the server. This avoids extra latency caused by packetloss, but could also make the problem worse.

cl_c2spps.desc: Reduces outgoing packet rates by dropping up to a third of outgoing packets.

cl_chatmode.desc:
0(nq) - everything is assumed to be a console command. prefix with 'say', or just use a messagemode bind
1(q3) - everything is assumed to be chat, unless its prefixed with a /
2(qw) - anything explicitly recognised as a command will be used as a command, anything unrecognised will be a chat message.
/ prefix is supported in all cases.
ctrl held when pressing enter always makes any implicit chat into team chat instead.

cl_countpendingpl.desc: If set to 1, packet loss percentages will show packets still in transit as lost, even if they might still be received.

cl_crypt_rcon.desc: Controls whether to send a hash instead of sending your rcon password as plain-text. Set to 1 for security, or 0 for backwards compatibility.\nYour command and any responses will still be sent as plain text.\nInstead, it is recommended to use rcon ONLY via dtls/tls/wss connections.

cl_defaultport.desc: The default port used to connect to servers.\nQW: , NQ: , Q2: , Q3: .

cl_demoreel.desc: When enabled, the engine will begin playing a demo loop on startup.

cl_dlemptyterminate.desc: Terminate downloads when reciving an empty download packet. This should help work around buggy mvdsv servers.

cl_download_csprogs.desc: Download updated client gamecode if available. Warning: If you clear this to avoid downloading vm code, you should also clear cl_download_packages.

cl_download_mapsrc.desc: Specifies an http location prefix for map downloads. EG: \"http://example.com/path/gamemaps/\"

cl_download_packages.desc: 0=Do not download packages simply because the server is using them. 1=Download and load packages as needed (does not affect games which do not use this package). 2=Do download and install permanently (use with caution!)

cl_download_redirection.desc: Follow download redirection to download packages instead of individual files. Also allows the server to send nearly arbitary download commands.\n2: allows redirection only to named packages files (and demos/*.mvd), which is a bit safer.

cl_download_wait.desc: 0=join the game before downloads have even finished (might be laggy). 1=wait for all downloads to complete before joining.

cl_downloads.desc: Allows you to block all automatic downloads.

cl_expsprite.desc: Display a central sprite in explosion effects. QuakeWorld typically does so, NQ mods should not (which is problematic when played with the qw protocol).

cl_fakeframes.desc: Slow GPU? Want to see higher framerates get reported! Unleash the power of the lie to see much higher framerates! Many people said it couldn't be done, that the people wouldn't accept it, but to hell with the neighsayers and non-believers! WE WANT BIGGER NUMBERS AND WE'RE DAMN WELL GONNA GET THEM!... For best results, combine with an external tool like fluid motion frames...

cl_fastaccel.desc: Begin moving at full speed instantly, instead of waiting a frame or so.

cl_fullpitch.desc: When set, attempts to unlimit the default view pitch. Note that some servers will screw over your angles if you use this, resulting in terrible gameplay, while some may merely clamp your angle serverside. This is also considered a cheat in quakeworld, ^1so this will not function there^7. For the equivelent in quakeworld, use serverinfo minpitch+maxpitch instead, which applies to all players fairly.

cl_hightrack.desc: Obsolete. If you want hightrack, use '[cl_]autotrack high' instead.

cl_iDrive.desc: Effectively releases movement keys when the opposing key is pressed. This avoids dead-time when both keys are pressed. This can be emulated with various scripts, but that's messy.

cl_idlefps.desc: This is the maximum framerate to attain while idle/paused/unfocused.

cl_legacystains.desc: WARNING: this cvar will default to 0 and later removed at some point

cl_lerp_driftbias.desc: Additional bias, can be set to a negative value to hold interpolation in the past.

cl_lerp_driftfrac.desc: Proportion of the latest time vs the older time to favour drifting towards.

cl_lerp_maxdistance.desc: Maximum distance that an entity may move between snapshots without being considered as having teleported.

cl_lerp_maxinterval.desc: Maximum interval between keyframes, in seconds. Larger values can result in entities drifting very slowly when they move sporadically.

cl_lerp_players.desc: Set this to make other players smoother, though it may increase effective latency. Affects only QuakeWorld.

cl_lerp_smooth.desc: If 2, will act as 1 when playing demos/singleplayer and otherwise act as if set to 0 (ie: deathmatch).\nIf 1, interpolation will run in the past, resulting in really smooth movement at the cost of latency (even on bunchy german ISDNs).\nIf 0, interpolation will be based upon packet arrival times and may judder due to packet loss.

cl_loopbackprotocol.desc: Which protocol to use for single-player/the internal client. Should be one of: qw, qwid, nqid, nq, fitz, bjp3, dp6, dp7, auto. If 'auto', will use qw protocols for qw mods, and nq protocols for nq mods.

cl_maxfps.desc: Sets the maximum allowed framerate. If you're using vsync or want to uncap framerates entirely then you should probably set this to 0. Set cl_yieldcpu 0 if you're trying to benchmark.

cl_maxfps_slop.desc: If a frame is delayed (eg because of poor system timer precision), this is how much sooner to pretend the frame happened (in milliseconds). If it is set too low then the average framerate will drop below the target, while too high may result in excessively fast frames.

cl_model_bobbing.desc: Makes rotating pickup items bob too.

cl_movement.desc: Specifies whether to send movement sequence info over DPP7 protocols (other protocols are unaffected). Unlike cl_nopred, this can result in different serverside behaviour.

cl_netfps.desc: Send up to this many packets to the server per second. The rate used is also limited by the server which usually forces a cap to this setting of 77. Low packet rates can result in extra extrapolation to try to hide the resulting latencies.

cl_nofake.desc: value 0: permits \\r chars in chat messages\nvalue 1: blocks all \\r chars\nvalue 2: allows \\r chars, but only from teammates

cl_nolerp.desc: Disables interpolation. If set, missiles/monsters will be show exactly what was last received, which will be jerky. Does not affect players. A value of 2 means 'interpolate only in single-player/coop'.

cl_nolerp_netquake.desc: Disables interpolation when connected to an NQ server. Does affect players, even the local player. You probably don't want to set this.

cl_parsewhitetext.desc: When parsing chat messages, enable support for messages like: red{white}red

cl_part_density_fade.desc: Specifies the distance over which ssqc pointparticles density fades from all to none. If this is set to 0 then particles will spawn at their normal density regardless of location on the map.

cl_part_density_fade_start.desc: Specifies the distance at which ssqc's pointparticles will start to get less dense.

cl_predict_extrapolate.desc: If 1, enables prediction based upon partial input frames which can change over time resulting in a swimmy feel but does not need to interpolate. If 0, prediction will stay in the past and thus use only completed frames. Interpolation will then be used to smooth movement.\nThis cvar only applies when video and input frames are independant (ie: cl_netfps is set).

cl_predict_players.desc: Clear this cvar to see ents exactly how they are on the server.

cl_predict_players_frac.desc: How much of other players to predict. Values less than 1 will help minimize overruns.

cl_predict_players_latency.desc: Push the player back according to your latency, to give a smooth consistent simulation of the server.

cl_predict_players_nudge.desc: An extra nudge of time, to cover video latency.

cl_predict_timenudge.desc: A debug feature. You should normally leave this as 0. Nudges local player prediction into the future if positive (resulting in extrapolation), or into the past if negative (resulting in laggy interpolation). Value is in seconds, so small decimals are required. This cvar applies even if input frames are tied to video frames.

cl_pure.desc:
0=standard quake rules.
1=clients should prefer files within packages present on the server.
2=clients should use *only* files within packages present on the server.
Due to quake 1.01/1.06 differences, a setting of 2 is only reliable with total conversions.
If sv_pure is set, the client will prefer the highest value set.

cl_queueimpulses.desc: Queues unsent impulses instead of replacing them. This avoids the need for extra wait commands (and the timing issues of such commands), but potentially increases latency and can cause scripts to be desynced with regard to buttons and impulses.

cl_r2g.desc: Uses progs/grenade.mdl instead of progs/missile.mdl when 1.

cl_rollalpha.desc: Controls the speed at which the view rolls according to sideways movement.

cl_rollangle.desc: Controls the maximum view should tilt while strafing.

cl_rollspeed.desc: Controls the speed required to reach cl_rollangle's tilt.

cl_run.desc: Enables autorun, inverting the state of the +speed key.

cl_sbaralpha.desc: Specifies the transparency of the status bar. Only Takes effect when cl_sbar is set to 2.

cl_sendchatstate.desc: Announce your chat state to the server in a privacy-violating kind of way. This allows other players to see your afk/at-console status.

cl_sendguid.desc: Send a randomly generated 'globally unique' id to servers, which can be used by servers for score rankings and stuff. Different servers will see different guids. Delete the 'qkey' file in order to appear as a different user.\nIf set to 2, all servers will see the same guid. Be warned that this can show other people the guid that you're using.

cl_serveraddress.desc: The address of the last server you connected to

cl_servername.desc: The hostname of the last server you connected to

cl_shownet.desc: Debugging var. 0 shows nothing. 1 shows incoming packet sizes. 2 shows individual messages. 3 shows entities too.

cl_smartjump.desc: Makes the jump button act as +moveup when in water. This is typically quieter and faster.

cl_solid_players.desc: Consider other players as solid for player prediction.

cl_splitscreen.desc: Enables splitscreen support. See also: allow_splitscreen, in_rawinput*, the \"p\" command.

cl_standardchat.desc: Disables auto colour coding in chat messages.

cl_standardmsg.desc: Disables auto colour coding in console prints.

cl_threadedphysics.desc: When set, client input frames are generated and sent on a worker thread

cl_truelightning.desc: Manipulate the end position of the player's own beams, to hide lag. Can be set to fractional values to reduce the effect.

cl_verify_urischeme.desc: 0: Do nothing.\n1: Check whether our protocol scheme is registered and prompt the user to register associations.\n2: Always re-register on every startup, without prompting. Sledgehammer style.

cl_voip_autogain.desc: Attempts to normalize your voice levels to a standard level. Useful for lazy people, but interferes with voice activation levels.

cl_voip_bitrate.desc: For codecs with non-specific bitrates, this specifies the target bitrate to use.

cl_voip_capturingvol.desc: Volume multiplier applied while capturing, to avoid your audio from being heard by others. Does not affect game volume when others speak (minimum of cl_voip_capturingvol and cl_voip_ducking is used).

cl_voip_codec.desc: 0: speex(@11khz). 1: raw. 2: opus. 3: speex(@8khz). 4: speex(@16). 5:speex(@32). 6: pcma. 7: pcmu.

cl_voip_ducking.desc: Scales game audio by this much when someone is talking to you. Does not affect your speaker volume when you speak (minimum of cl_voip_capturingvol and cl_voip_ducking is used).

cl_voip_micamp.desc: Amplifies your microphone when using voip.

cl_voip_noisefilter.desc: Enable the use of the noise cancelation filter.

cl_voip_play.desc: Enables voip playback. Value is a volume scaler.

cl_voip_send.desc:
Sends voice-over-ip data to the server whenever it is set.
0: only send voice if +voip is pressed.
1: voice activation.
2: constantly send.
+4: Do not send to game, only to rtp sessions.

cl_voip_showmeter.desc: Shows your speech volume above the standard hud. 0=hide, 1=show when transmitting, 2=ignore voice-activation disable

cl_voip_test.desc: If 1, enables you to hear your own voice directly, bypassing the server and thus without networking latency, but is fine for checking audio levels. Note that sv_voip_echo can be set if you want to include latency and packetloss considerations, but setting that cvar requires server admin access and is thus much harder to use.

cl_voip_vad_delay.desc: Keeps sending voice data for this many seconds after voice activation would normally stop

cl_voip_vad_threshhold.desc: This is the threshhold for voice-activation-detection when sending voip data

cl_vrui_force.desc: Force the use of VR UIs, even with no VR headset active.

cl_vrui_lock.desc: Controls how the UI is positioned when using VR/XR. 0: Repositioned infront of the head when the console/menus are toggled. 1: Locked infront of the reference position (which may require the user to turn around to find it).

cl_weaponforgetorder.desc: The 'weapon' command will lock in its weapon choice, instead of choosing a different weapon between select+fire.

cl_weaponhide.desc:
HACK: Attempt to switch weapon to another in order to cheat your killer out of any possible weapon upgrades.
0: original behaviour
1: switch away when +attack/+fire is released
2: switch away only in deathmatch

cl_weaponhide_preference.desc: The weapon you would like to try to switch to when cl_weaponhide is active

cl_yieldcpu.desc: Attempt to yield between frames. This can resolve issues with certain drivers and background software, but can mean less consistant frame times. Will reduce power consumption/heat generation so should be set on laptops or similar (over-hot/battery powered) devices.

com_fullgamename.desc: The filesystem is trying to run this game

com_highlightcolor.desc: ANSI colour to be used for highlighted text, used when com_parseutf8 is active.

com_parseutf8.desc: Interpret console messages/playernames/etc as UTF-8. Requires special fonts. -1=iso 8859-1. 0=quakeascii(chat uses high chars). 1=utf8, revert to ascii on decode errors. 2=utf8 ignoring errors

com_protocolname.desc: The protocol game name used for dpmaster queries. For compatibility with DP, you can set this to 'DarkPlaces-Quake' in order to be listed in DP's master server, and to list DP servers.

com_protocolversion.desc: The protocol version used for dpmaster queries.

con_logcenterprint.desc:
Specifies whether to print centerprints on the console.
0: never
1: single-player or coop only.
2: always.

con_stayhidden.desc:
0: allow console to pounce on the user
1: console stays hidden unless explicitly invoked
2:toggleconsole command no longer works
3: shift+escape key no longer works

con_textfont.desc: Specifies the font file to use. a value such as FONT:ALTFONT specifies an alternative font to be used when ^^a is used.\nWhen using TTF fonts, you will likely need to scale text to at least 150% - vid_conautoscale 1.5 will do this.\nTTF fonts may be loaded from your windows directory. \'gl_font cour?col=1,1,1:couri?col=0,1,0\' loads eg: c:\\windows\\fonts\\cour.ttf, and uses the italic version of courier for alternative text, with specific colour tints.

con_textsize.desc: Resize the console text to be a different height, scaled separately from the hud. The value is the height in (virtual) pixels.

con_window.desc: States whether the console should be a floating window as in source engine games, or a top-of-the-screen-only thing.

contrast.desc: Scales colour values linearly to make your screen easier to see. Setting this to anything but 1 without hardware gamma will reduce your framerates a little.

crosshaircorrect.desc: Moves the crosshair around to represent the impact point of a weapon positioned below the actual view position.

crosshairimage.desc: Enables the use of an external/custom crosshair image

d_lodbias.desc: Biases choice of mipmap levels. Positive values will give more blury textures, while negative values will give crisper images (but will also give some mid-surface aliasing artifacts).

d_mipcap.desc: Specifies the range of mipmap levels to use.

developer.desc: Enables the spewing of additional developer/debugging messages. 2 will give even more spam, much of it unwanted.

dpcompat_console.desc: Enables hacks to emulate DP's console.

dpcompat_csqcinputeventtypes.desc: Specifies the first csqc input event that the mod does not recognise. This should never have been a thing, but some mods are simply too buggy.

dpcompat_findradiusarealinks.desc: Use the world collision info to accelerate findradius instead of looping through every single entity. May actually be slower for large radiuses, or fail to find entities which have not been linked properly with setorigin.

dpcompat_nofloodfill.desc: Disables the q1mdl floodfill. Setting this to 1 may result in blue seams on the vanilla quake models.

dpcompat_nopremulpics.desc: By default FTE uses premultiplied alpha for hud/2d images, while DP does not (which results in halos with low-res content). Unfortunately DDS files would need to be recompressed, resulting in visible issues.

dpcompat_nopreparse.desc: Xonotic uses svc_tempentity with unknowable lengths mixed with other data that needs to be translated. This cvar disables any attempt to translate or pre-parse network messages, including disabling nq/qw cross compatibility. NOTE: because preparsing will be disabled, messages might not get backbuffered correctly if too much reliable data is written.

dpcompat_noretouchground.desc: Prevents entities that are already standing on an entity from touching the same entity again.

dpcompat_precachesoundhack.desc: Changes the behaviour of only the ssqc's precache_sound to return a precache index. precache_model and csqc's precaches are unchanged.

dpcompat_skinfiles.desc: When set, uses a nodraw shader for any unmentioned surfaces.

dpcompat_smallerfonts.desc: Mimics DP's behaviour of using a smaller font size than was actually requested.

dpcompat_strcat_limit.desc: When set, cripples strcat (and related function) string lengths to the value specified.\nSet to 16383 to replicate DP's limit, otherwise leave as 0 to avoid limits.

drate.desc: A rough measure of the bandwidth to try to use while downloading (in bytes per second).

dtls_psk_hint.desc: For DTLS-PSK handshakes. This specifies the public server identity.

dtls_psk_key.desc: For DTLS-PSK handshakes. This specifies the hexadecimal key which must match between client+server. Will only be used when client+server's hint settings match.

dtls_psk_user.desc: For DTLS-PSK handshakes. This specifies the username to use when the client+server's hints match.

edit_addcr.desc: make sure that each line ends with a \\r (on save). Empty will be assumed to be 1 on windows and 0 otherwise.

ezcompat_markup.desc: Attempt compatibility with ezquake's text markup.0: disabled.\n1: Handle markup ampersand markup.\n2: Handle chevron markup (only in echo commands, for config compat, because its just too unreliable otherwise).

ffov.desc: Allows you to set a specific field of view for when a custom projection is specified. If empty, will use regular fov cvar, which might get messy.

filterban.desc: If 0, players will be kicked by default unless there is a rule that allows them. Also affects the default action of addip.

fov.desc: field of vision, 1-170 degrees, standard fov is 90, nquake defaults to 108.

fraglog_details.desc:
Bitmask
1: killer+killee names.
2: killer+killee teams
4:timestamp.
8:killer weapon
16:killer+killee guid.
For compatibility, use 1(vanilla) or 7(mvdsv).

fraglog_public.desc: Enables support for connectionless fraglog requests

fs_basepath.desc: Provided for Q2/Q3 compat. System path of the base directory.

fs_cache.desc: 0: Do individual lookups.\n1: Scan all files for accelerated lookups. This provides a performance boost on windows and avoids case sensitivity issues on linux.\n2: like 1, but don't bother checking for external changes (avoiding the cost of rebuild the cache).

fs_game.desc: Provided for Q2 compat. Contains the subdir of the current mod.

fs_gamepath.desc: Provided for Q2/Q3 compat. System path of the active gamedir.

fs_hidesyspaths.desc: 0: Show system paths in console prints that might appear in screenshots or video capture.\n1: Replace the start of filenames in console prints with generic prefixes that cannot leak private info like your operating system's user name.

fs_homepath.desc: Provided for Q2/Q3 compat. System path of the base directory.

fs_noreexec.desc: Disables automatic re-execing configs on gamedir switches.\nThis means your cvar defaults etc may be from the wrong mod, and cfg_save will leave that stuff corrupted!

fs_packageprioritisation.desc: Favours the package that is:\n0: Most recently modified\n1: Is alphabetically last (favour z over a, 9 over 0).

gamma.desc: Controls how bright the screen is. Setting this to anything but 1 without hardware gamma requires glsl support and can noticably harm your framerate.

gl_affinemodels.desc: Use affine texture sampling for models. This replicates software rendering's distortions.

gl_blacklist_generatemipmap.desc: Self-generate mipmaps, instead of letting the graphics driver do it.

gl_blacklist_texture_compression.desc: When enabled, blocks recognition of all compressed-texture formats. Does NOT block support for gl3 texture types like e5bgr9 nor rgba16f.

gl_blendsprites.desc:
Specifies how sprites are blended.
0: Alpha tested.
1: Premultiplied blend.
2: Additive blend.

gl_compress.desc: Enable automatic texture compression even for textures which are not pre-compressed.

gl_conback.desc: Specifies which conback shader/image to use. The Quake fallback is gfx/conback.lmp

gl_driver.desc: Specifies the graphics driver name to load. This is typically a filename. Blank for default.

gl_font.desc: Specifies the font file to use. a value such as FONT:ALTFONT specifies an alternative font to be used when ^^a is used.\nWhen using TTF fonts, you will likely need to scale text to at least 150% - vid_conautoscale 1.5 will do this.\nTTF fonts may be loaded from your windows directory. \'gl_font cour?col=1,1,1:couri?col=0,1,0\' loads eg: c:\\windows\\fonts\\cour.ttf, and uses the italic version of courier for alternative text, with specific colour tints.

gl_immutable_buffers.desc: Controls whether to use immutable GPU memory allocations for static OpenGL vertex buffers. This potentially means less work for the drivers and thus higher framerates.

gl_immutable_textures.desc: Controls whether to use immutable GPU memory allocations for OpenGL textures. This potentially means less work for the drivers and thus higher framerates.

gl_lerpimages.desc: Enables smoother resampling for images which are not power-of-two, when the drivers do not support non-power-of-two textures.

gl_lightmap_average.desc: Determine lightmap values based upon the center of the polygon. This will give a more buggy look, quite probably.

gl_lightmap_nearest.desc: Use nearest sampling for lightmaps. This will give a more blocky look. Meaningless when gl_lightmap_average is enabled.

gl_max_size.desc: Specifies the maximum texture size that the engine may use. Textures larger than this will be downsized. Clamped by the value the driver supports.

gl_maxdist.desc: The distance of the far clip plane. If set to 0, some fancy maths will be used to place it at an infinite distance.

gl_menutint_shader.desc: Controls the use of GLSL to desaturate the background when drawing the menu, like quake's dos software renderer used to do before the ugly dithering of winquake.

gl_mindist.desc: Distance to the near clip plane. Smaller values may damage depth precision, high values can potentialy be used to see through walls...

gl_nocolors.desc: Ignores player colours and skins, reducing texture memory usage at the cost of not knowing whether you're killing your team mates.

gl_nohwblend.desc: If 1, don't use hardware gamma ramps for transient effects that change each frame (does not affect long-term effects like holding quad or underwater tints).

gl_overbright_models.desc: Doubles the brightness of models, to match QuakeSpasm's misfeature of the same name.

gl_part_flame.desc: Enable particle emitting from models. Mainly used for torch and flame effects.

gl_pbolightmaps.desc: Controls whether to use PBOs for streaming lightmap updates. This prevents CPU stalls while the driver reads out the lightmap data (lightmap updates are still not free though).

gl_picmip.desc: Reduce world/model texture sizes by some exponential factor.

gl_picmip2d.desc: Reduce hud/menu texture sizes by some exponential factor.

gl_picmip_other.desc: Effectively added to gl_picmip for the purposes of model textures.

gl_picmip_sprites.desc: Effectively added to gl_picmip for the purposes of sprite textures.

gl_picmip_world.desc: Effectively added to gl_picmip for the purposes of world textures.

gl_polyblend.desc: Controls whether temporary whole-screen colour changes should be honoured or not. Change gl_cshiftpercent if you want to adjust the intensity.\nThis does not affect v_cshift commands sent from the server.

gl_polyblend_edgesize.desc: This constrains colour shifts to the edge of the screen, with the value specifying the size of those borders.

gl_shadeq1_name.desc: Rename all surfaces from quake1 bsps using this pattern for the purposes of shader names.

gl_skyboxdist.desc: The distance of the skybox. If 0, the engine will determine it based upon the far clip plane distance.

gl_texture_anisotropy.desc: Allows for higher quality textures on surfaces that slope away from the camera (like the floor). Set to 16 or something. Only supported with trilinear filtering.

gl_texturemode.desc:
Specifies how world/model textures appear. Typically 3 letters eg nll or lll.
First letter can be l(inear) or n(earest) and says how to upscale low-res textures (n for the classic look - often favoured for embedded textures, l for blurry - best for high-res textures).
The middle letter can be set to '.' to disable mipmaps, or n for ugly banding with distance, or l for smooth mipmap transitions.
The third letter says what to do when the texture is too high resolution, and should generally be set to 'l' to reduce sparkles including when aiming for the classic lego look.

gl_texturemode2d.desc: Specifies how 2d images are sampled. format is a 3-tupple

gl_workaround_ati_shadersource.desc: Work around ATI driver bugs in the glShaderSource function. Can safely be enabled with other drivers too.

hand.desc:
For gamecode to know which hand to fire from.
0: Right
1: Left
2: Chest

ignore_flood.desc:
Provides a way to reduce inbound spam from flooding out your chat (dupe messages are ignored).
0: No inbound flood protection.
1: Duplicate non-team messages will be filtered.
2: ALL duplicate messages will be filtered

ignore_flood_duration.desc: Time limit for inbound messages to be considered duplicates.

ignore_opponents.desc:
0: Don't ignore chat from enemies.
1: Always ignore chat from opponents (note: can also ignore f_ruleset checks).
2: Ignore chat from opponents only during a match (requires servers that actually reports match state).

ignore_spec.desc: 0: Never ignore spectators.\n1: Ignore spectators only when playing.\n2: Always ignore spectators even when spectating.

in_dinput.desc: Enables the use of dinput for mouse movements

in_forceseat.desc: Overrides the device identifiers to control a specific client from any device. This can be used for debugging mods, where you only have one keyboard/mouse.

in_nonstandarddeadkeys.desc: Discard input events that result in multiple keys. Only the last key will be used. This results in behaviour that differs from eg notepad. To use a dead key, press it twice instead of the dead key followed by space.

in_rawinput.desc: Enables rawinput support for mice in XP onwards. Rawinput permits independant device identification (ie: splitscreen clients can each have their own mouse)

in_rawinput_keyboard.desc: Enables rawinput support for keyboards in XP onwards as well as just mice.

in_rawinput_rdp.desc: Activate Remote Desktop Protocol devices too.

in_skipplayerone.desc: Do not auto-assign joysticks/game-controllers to the first player. Requires in_restart to take effect.

in_vraim.desc: When set to 1, the 'view' angle sent to the server is controlled by your vr headset instead of separately. This is for fallback behaviour and blocks mouse+joy+gamepad aiming.

in_xinput.desc: Enables the use of xinput for controllers.\nNote that if you have a headset plugged in, that headset will be used for audio playback if no specific audio device is configured.

ipautodump.desc: Enables dumping the 'iplog.txt' file, which contains a log of usernames seen for a given IP, which is useful for detecting fake-nicks.

joyadvaxisr.desc: Provides a way to remap each joystick/controller axis.\nShould be set to one of: moveforward, moveback, lookup, lookdown, turnleft, turnright, moveleft, moveright, moveup, movedown, rollleft, rollright

joyadvaxisr_scale.desc: Because joyadvaxisx etc can be added together, this provides a way to rescale or invert an individual axis without affecting another with the same action.

joyadvaxisu.desc: Provides a way to remap each joystick/controller axis.\nShould be set to one of: moveforward, moveback, lookup, lookdown, turnleft, turnright, moveleft, moveright, moveup, movedown, rollleft, rollright

joyadvaxisu_scale.desc: Because joyadvaxisx etc can be added together, this provides a way to rescale or invert an individual axis without affecting another with the same action.

joyadvaxisv.desc: Provides a way to remap each joystick/controller axis.\nShould be set to one of: moveforward, moveback, lookup, lookdown, turnleft, turnright, moveleft, moveright, moveup, movedown, rollleft, rollright

joyadvaxisv_scale.desc: Because joyadvaxisx etc can be added together, this provides a way to rescale or invert an individual axis without affecting another with the same action.

joyadvaxisx.desc: Provides a way to remap each joystick/controller axis.\nShould be set to one of: moveforward, moveback, lookup, lookdown, turnleft, turnright, moveleft, moveright, moveup, movedown, rollleft, rollright

joyadvaxisx_scale.desc: Because joyadvaxisx etc can be added together, this provides a way to rescale or invert an individual axis without affecting another with the same action.

joyadvaxisy.desc: Provides a way to remap each joystick/controller axis.\nShould be set to one of: moveforward, moveback, lookup, lookdown, turnleft, turnright, moveleft, moveright, moveup, movedown, rollleft, rollright

joyadvaxisy_scale.desc: Because joyadvaxisx etc can be added together, this provides a way to rescale or invert an individual axis without affecting another with the same action.

joyadvaxisz.desc: Provides a way to remap each joystick/controller axis.\nShould be set to one of: moveforward, moveback, lookup, lookdown, turnleft, turnright, moveleft, moveright, moveup, movedown, rollleft, rollright

joyadvaxisz_scale.desc: Because joyadvaxisx etc can be added together, this provides a way to rescale or invert an individual axis without affecting another with the same action.

joyexponent.desc: Scales joystick/controller sensitivity non-linearly to increase precision in the center.\nA value of 1 is linear.

joypitchsensitivity.desc: Scaler value for the controller when it is at its most extreme value

joypitchthreshold.desc: Values reported near the center of the analog joystick/controller are often erroneous and undesired.\nThe joystick threshholds are how much of the total values to ignore.

joyradialdeadzone.desc:
Treat controller dead zones as a pair, rather than per-axis.
0: treat joystick axis independantly (square).
1: treat the axis together, radially.
2: do not handle deadzones (prefiltered).

joyrollsensitivity.desc: Scaler value for the controller when it is at its most extreme value

joyrollthreshold.desc: Values reported near the center of the analog joystick/controller are often erroneous and undesired.\nThe joystick threshholds are how much of the total values to ignore.

joyyawsensitivity.desc: Scaler value for the controller when it is at its most extreme value

joyyawthreshold.desc: Values reported near the center of the analog joystick/controller are often erroneous and undesired.\nThe joystick threshholds are how much of the total values to ignore.

lang.desc: This cvar contains the language_dialect code of your language, used to find localisation strings.

log_developer.desc: Enables logging of console prints when set to 1. Otherwise unimportant messages will not fill up your log files.

log_readable.desc:
Bitfield describing what to convert/strip. If 0, exact byte representation will be used.
&1: Dequakify text.
&2: Strip special markup.
&4: Strip ansi control codes.

lookspring.desc: Recentre the camera when the mouse-look is released.

m_accel.desc: Values >0 will amplify mouse movement proportional to velocity. Small values have great effect. A lot of good Quake Live players use around the 0.1-0.2 mark, but this depends on your mouse CPI and polling rate.

m_accel_offset.desc: Used when m_accel_style is 1.\nAcceleration will not be active until the mouse movement exceeds this speed (counts per millisecond). Negative values are supported, which has the effect of causing higher rates of acceleration to happen at lower velocities.

m_accel_power.desc: Used when m_accel_style is 1.\nValues 1 or below are dumb. 2 is linear and the default. 99% of accel users use this. Above 2 begins to amplify exponentially and you will get more acceleration at higher velocities. Great if you want low accel for slow movements, and high accel for fast movements. Good in combination with a sensitivity cap.

m_accel_senscap.desc: Used when m_accel_style is 1.\nSets an upper limit on the amplified mouse movement. Great for tuning acceleration around lower velocities while still remaining in control of fast motion such as flicking.

m_accel_style.desc: 1 = Quake Live mouse acceleration, 0 = Old style accelertion.

m_forcewheel.desc: 0: ignore mousewheels in apis where it is abiguous.\n1: Use mousewheel when it is treated as a third axis. Motion above a threshold is ignored, to avoid issues with an unknown threshold.\n2: Like 1, but excess motion is retained. The threshold specifies exact z-axis distance per notice.

m_forcewheel_threshold.desc: Mousewheel graduations smaller than this will not trigger mousewheel deltas.

m_longpressthreshold.desc: How long to press for it to register as a long press (touchscreens).

m_slidethreshold.desc: How far your finger needs to move to be considered a slide event (touchscreens).

m_touchmajoraxis.desc: When using a touchscreen, use only the major axis for strafing.

m_touchstrafe.desc: 0: entire screen changes angles only.\n1: right hand side controls strafing.\n2:left hand side strafes.

map_autoopenportals.desc: When set to 1, force-opens all area portals. Normally these start closed and are opened by doors when they move, but this requires the gamecode to signal this.

mapname.desc: Cvar that holds the short name of the current map, for scripting type stuff

mastervolume.desc: Additional multiplier for all other sounds.

maxclients.desc: Specify the maximum number of players allowed on the server at once. Can be changed mid-map.

maxspectators.desc: Specify the maximum number of spectators allowed on the server at once. Can be changed mid-map.

mod_external_vis.desc: Attempt to load .vis patches for quake maps, allowing transparent water to work properly.

mod_h2holey_bugged.desc: Hexen2's holey-model flag uses index 0 as transparent (and additionally 255 in gl, due to a bug). GLQuake engines tend to have bugs that use ONLY index 255, resulting in a significant compatibility issue that can be resolved only with this shitty cvar hack.

mod_halftexel.desc: Offset texture coords by a half-texel, for compatibility with glquake and the majority of engine forks.

mod_lightpoint_distance.desc: This is the maximum distance to trace when searching for a ground surface for lighting info on map formats without light more fancy lighting info. Use 2048 for full compat with Quake.

mod_lightscale_broken.desc: When active, replicates a bug from vanilla - the radius of r_dynamic lights is scaled by per-surface texture scale rather than using actual distance.

mod_litsprites_force.desc: If set to 1, sprites will be lit according to world lighting (including rtlights), like Tenebrae. Ideally use EF_ADDITIVE or EF_FULLBRIGHT to make emissive sprites instead.

mod_loadmappackages.desc: Load additional content embedded within bsp files.

mod_map_texscale.desc: Defines the scale of texture texels. Use 1 for quake+quake2 maps, and 0.5 for quake3 maps.

mod_md3flags.desc: The flags field of md3s was never officially defined. If this is set to 1, the flags will be treated identically to mdl files. Otherwise they will be ignored. Naturally, this is required to provide rotating pickups in quake.

mod_md5_singleanimation.desc: When loading an md5mesh file, also attempt to load an .md5anim file, and unpack it into individual poses. Use 0 for mods that will be precaching their own md5anims for use with skeletal objects.

mod_nomipmap.desc: Disables the use of mipmaps on quake1 mdls, consistent with its original software renderer.

mod_obj_orientation.desc:
Controls how the model's axis are interpreted.
0: x=forward, z=up (Quake)
1: x=forward, y=up
2: z=forward, y=up

mod_precache.desc:
Controls when models are loaded.
0: Load them only when they're actually needed.
1: Load them upfront.
2: Lazily load them to shorten load times at the risk of brief stuttering during only the start of the map.

mod_terrain_defaulttexture.desc: Newly created terrain tiles will use this texture. This should generally be updated by the terrain editor.

mod_terrain_networked.desc: Terrain edits are networked. Clients will download sections on demand, and servers will notify clients of changes.

mod_terrain_savever.desc: Which terrain section version to write if terrain was edited.

mod_terrain_shadow_dist.desc: How far rays should be cast in order to look for occlusing geometry.

mod_terrain_shadows.desc: Cast rays to determine whether parts of the terrain should be in shadow.

mod_terrain_sundir.desc: The direction of the sun (vector will be normalised).

mod_warnmodels.desc: Warn if any models failed to load. Set to 0 if your mod is likely to lack optional models (like its in development).

msg.desc: Filter console prints/messages. Only functions on QuakeWorld servers. 0=pickup messages. 1=death messages. 2=critical messages. 3=chat.

msg_filter.desc: Filter out chat messages: 0=neither. 1=broadcast chat. 2=team chat. 3=all chat.

msg_filter_frags.desc: Prevents frag messages from appearing on the console.

msg_filter_pickups.desc: Prevents pickup messages from appearing on the console. This would normally be filtered by 'msg 1', but nq servers cannot respect that (nor nq mods running in qw servers).

net_compress.desc: Enables huffman compression of network packets.

net_dns_ipv4.desc: If 0, disables dns resolution of names to ipv4 addresses (removing any associated error messages). Also hides ipv4 addresses in address:port listings.

net_dns_ipv6.desc: If 0, disables dns resolution of names to ipv6 addresses (removing any associated error messages). Also hides ipv6 addresses in address:port listings.

net_enable_.desc: If enabled, accept connection requests from the quake2-remaster engine on our listening udp ports.\nNote that this defaults to disabled due to it being highly vulnerable to applification attacks.

net_enable_dtls.desc:
Controls serverside dtls support.
0: dtls blocked, not advertised.
1: clientside choice.
2: used where possible (recommended setting).
3: disallow non-dtls clients (sv_port_tcp should be eg tls://[::]:27500 to also disallow unencrypted tcp connections).

net_enable_http.desc: If enabled, tcp ports will accept inbound http clients, potentially serving large files which could distrupt gameplay (This does not affect outgoing http(s) requests).

net_enable_qizmo.desc: Enables serverside support for 'connect tcp://foo' or 'connect tls://foo' (with net_enable_tls), as well as qizmo's tcp connections and compatibles.

net_enable_qtv.desc:
Controls whether inbound qtv requests will be honoured (both proxies and clients using qtvplay).
0: Don't accept qtv connections.
1: Accept connections.
2: Accept qtv connections only from host-scopped addresses (read: 127.*.*.*, ::1, or unix sockets).

net_enable_rtcbroker.desc: If 1, tcp ports will accept websocket connections from clients trying to broker direct webrtc connections. This should be low traffic, but might involve a lot of mostly-idle connections.

net_enable_tls.desc: If enabled, binary data sent to a non-tls tcp port will be interpretted as a tls handshake (enabling https or wss over the same tcp port.

net_enable_websockets.desc: If enabled, tcp ports will accept websocket game clients.

net_enabled.desc: If 0, disables all network access, including name resolution and socket creation. Does not affect loopback/internal connections.

net_fakeloss.desc: Simulates packetloss in both receiving and sending, on a scale from 0 to 1.

net_hybriddualstack.desc: Uses hybrid ipv4+ipv6 sockets where possible. Not supported on xp or below.

net_ice_allowmdns.desc: Boolean. When set to 0, prevents the use of multicast-dns to obtain candidates using random numbers instead of revealing private network info.

net_ice_allowstun.desc: Boolean. When set to 0, prevents the use of stun to determine our public address (does not prevent connecting to our peer's server-reflexive candidates).

net_ice_allowturn.desc: Boolean. When set to 0, prevents registration of turn connections (does not prevent connecting to our peer's relay candidates).

net_ice_broker.desc: This is the default broker we attempt to connect through when using 'sv_public /foo' or 'connect /foo'.

net_ice_debug.desc: 0: Hide messy details.\n1: Show new candidates.\n2: Show each connectivity test.

net_ice_exchangeprivateips.desc: Boolean. When set to 0, hides private IP addresses from your peers - only addresses determined from the other side of your router will be shared. You should only need to set this to 1 if mdns is unavailable.

net_ice_relayonly.desc: Boolean. When set to 1, blocks reporting non-relay local candidates, does not attempt to connect to remote candidates other than via a relay.

net_ice_servers.desc: A space-separated list of ICE servers, eg stun:host.example:3478 or turn:host.example:3478?user=foo?auth=blah

net_ice_usewebrtc.desc: Use webrtc's extra overheads rather than simple ICE. This makes packets larger and is slower to connect, but is compatible with the web port.

net_mtu.desc: Specifies a maximum udp payload size, above which packets will be fragmented. If routers all worked properly this could be some massive value, and some massive value may work really nicely for lans. Use smaller values than the default if you're connecting through nested tunnels through routers that fail with IP fragmentation.

nosound.desc: Disable all sound from the engine. Cannot be overriden by configs or anything if set via the -nosound commandline argument.

pext_ezquake_nochunks.desc: Prevents ezquake clients from being able to use the chunked download extension. This sidesteps numerous ezquake issues, and will make downloads slower but more robust.

pext_ezquake_verfortrans.desc: ezQuake does not implement PEXT_TRANS properly. This is the version of ezquake required for PEXT_TRANS to be allowed. This was still broken when I wrote this description, hence the large value.

pext_predinfo.desc: Enables some extra things to support prediction over NQ protocols.

pext_replacementdeltas.desc: Enables the use of alternative nack-based entity deltas

pkg_autoupdate.desc:
Controls autoupdates, can only be changed via the downloads menu.
0: off.
1: enabled (stable only).
2: enabled (unstable).
Note that autoupdate will still prompt the user to actually apply the changes.

plug_loaddefault.desc:
0: Load plugins only via explicit plug_load commands
1: Load built-in plugins and those selected via the package manager
2: Scan for misc plugins, loading all that can be found, but not built-ins.
3: Scan for plugins, and then load any built-ins

plug_sbar.desc:
Controls whether plugins are allowed to draw the hud, rather than the engine (when allowed by csqc). This is typically used to permit the ezhud plugin without needing to bother unloading it.
=0: never use hud plugins.
&1: Use hud plugins in deathmatch.
&2: Use hud plugins in singleplayer/coop.
=3: Always use hud plugins (when loaded).

pm_airstep.desc: Allows players to step up while jumping. This makes stairs more graceful but also increases potential jump heights.

pm_autobunny.desc: Players will continue jumping without needing to release the jump button.

pm_bunnyfriction.desc: Replicates NQ behaviour, ensuring that there's at least a frame of friction while jumping - friction is proportional to tick rate.

pm_bunnyspeedcap.desc: 0 or 1, ish. If the player is traveling faster than this speed while turning, their velocity will be gracefully reduced to match their current maxspeed. You can still rocket-jump to gain high velocity, but turning will reduce your speed back to the max. This can be used to disable bunny hopping.

pm_edgefriction.desc: Increases friction when about to walk over a cliff, so you're less likely to plummet by mistake. When empty defaults to 2, but uses a tracebox instead of a traceline to detect the drop.

pm_flyfriction.desc: Amount of friction that applies in fly or 6dof mode. Empty means 4.

pm_noround.desc: Disables player prediction snapping, in a way that cannot be reliably predicted but may be needed to avoid map bugs.

pm_pground.desc: Use persisten onground state instead of recalculating every frame.Do NOT use with nq mods, as most nq mods will interfere with onground state, resulting in glitches.

pm_slidefix.desc: Fixes an issue when walking down slopes (ie: so they act more like slopes and not a series of steps)

pm_slidyslopes.desc: Replicates NQ behaviour, where players will slowly slide down ramps. Generally requires 'pm_noround 1' too, otherwise the effect rounds to nothing.

pm_stepdown.desc: Causes physics to stick to the ground, instead of constantly losing traction while going down steps.

pm_stepheight.desc: If empty, the value  will be used instead. This is the size of the step you can step up or down.

pm_walljump.desc: Allows the player to bounce off walls while arborne.

pm_watersinkspeed.desc: This is the speed that players will sink at while inactive in water. Empty means 60.

pr_allowbutton1.desc: The button1 field is believed to have been intended to work with the +use command, but it was never hooked up. In NetQuake, this field was often repurposed for other things as it was not otherwise used (and cannot be removed without breaking the crc), while third-party QuakeWorld engines did decide to implement it as believed was intended. As a result, this cvar only applies to QuakeWorld mods and a value of 1 is only likely to cause issues with NQ mods that were ported to QW.

pr_autocreatecvars.desc: Implicitly create any cvars that don't exist when read.

pr_compatabilitytest.desc: Only enables builtins if the extension they are part of was queried.

pr_debugger.desc: When enabled, QC errors and debug events will enable step-by-step tracing.

pr_droptofloorunits.desc: Distance that droptofloor is allowed to drop to be considered successul.

pr_enable_profiling.desc: Enables profiling support. Will run more slowly. Change the map and then use the profile_ssqc/profile_csqc commands to see the results.

pr_enable_uriget.desc: Allows gamecode to make direct http requests

pr_engine.desc: This cvar exists so that the menuqc is able to determine which engine-specific settings/values to list/suggest. It must not be used to detect formal QC extensions/builtins. Use checkextension/checkbuiltin/checkcommand for that.

pr_ext_dp_qc_getsurface.desc: Set to 0 to block detection of the extension

pr_fixbrokenqccarrays.desc:
As part of its nq/qw/h2/csqc support, FTE remaps QC fields to match an internal order. This is a faster way to handle extended fields. However, some QCCs are buggy and don't report all field defs.
0: do nothing. QCC must be well behaved.
1: Duplicate engine fields, remap the ones we can to known offsets. This is sufficient for QCCX/FrikQCC mods that use hardcoded or even occasional calculated offsets (fixes ktpro).
2: Scan the mod for field accessing instructions, and assume those are the fields (and that they don't alias non-fields). This can be used to work around gmqcc's WTFs (fixes xonotic).

pr_gc_threaded.desc: Says whether to use a separate thread for tempstring garbage collections. This avoids main-thread stalls but at the expense of more memory usage.

pr_imitatemvdsv.desc: Enables mvdsv-specific builtins, and fakes identifiers so that mods made for mvdsv can run properly and with the full feature set.

pr_maxedicts.desc: Maximum number of entities spawnable on the map at once. Low values will crash the server on some maps/mods. High values will result in excessive memory useage (see pr_ssqc_memsize). Illegible server messages may occur with old/other clients above 32k. FTE's network protocols have a maximum at a little over 4 million. Please don't ever make a mod that actually uses that many...

pr_no_parsecommand.desc: Provides a way around invalid mod usage of SV_ParseClientCommand, eg xonotic.

pr_no_playerphysics.desc: Prevents support of the 'SV_PlayerPhysics' QC function. This allows servers to prevent needless breakage of player prediction.

pr_nonetaccess.desc: Block all direct access to network buffers (the writebyte builtin and friends will ignore the call).

pr_precachepic_slow.desc: Legacy setting. Should be set to 0 where supported.

pr_sourcedir.desc: Subdirectory where your qc source is located. Used by the internal compiler and qc debugging functionality.

pr_ssqc_memsize.desc: The ammount of memory available to the QC vm. This has a theoretical maximum of 1gb, but that value can only really be used in 64bit builds. -1 will attempt to use some conservative default, but you may need to increase it. Consider also clearing pr_fixbrokenqccarrays if you need to change this cvar.

pr_tempstringcount.desc: Obsolete. Set to 16 if you want to recycle+reuse the same 16 tempstring references and break lots of mods.

q3bsp_ignorestyles.desc: Ignores multiple lightstyles in Raven's q3bsp variant(and derivatives) for better batch/rendering performance.

q3bsp_mergelightmaps.desc: Specifies whether to merge lightmaps into atlases in order to boost performance. Unfortunately this breaks tcgen on lightmap passes - if you care, set this to 0.

q3bsp_surf_meshcollision_flag.desc: The surfaceparm flag(s) that enables q3bsp trisoup collision

q3bsp_surf_meshcollision_force.desc: Force mesh-based collisions on all q3bsp trisoup surfaces.

qtv_maxstreams.desc: This is the maximum number of QTV clients/proxies that may be directly connected to the server. If empty then there is no limit. 0 disallows any streaming.

r_bloom.desc: Enables bloom (light bleeding from bright objects). Fractional values reduce the amount shown.

r_bloom_downsize.desc: Technically more correct with a value of 1, but you probably won't notice.

r_bloom_filter.desc: Controls how bright the image must get before it will bloom (3 separate values, in RGB order).

r_bloom_initialscale.desc: Initial scaling factor for bloom. should be either 1 or 0.5

r_bloom_retain.desc: How much of the regular scene to retain when bloom is active.

r_bloom_size.desc: Target bloom kernel size (assuming a video width of 320).

r_bluelight_colour.desc: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_BLUE effects (typically used for quad-damage in quakeworld)

r_bouncysparks.desc: Enables particle interaction with world surfaces, allowing for bouncy particles, stains, and decals.

r_brightlight_colour.desc: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_BRIGHTLIGHT effects (unused in vanilla quake).

r_clutter_density.desc: Scaler for clutter counts. 0 disables clutter completely.\nClutter requires shaders with 'fte_clutter MODEL SPACING SCALEMIN SCALEMAX ZOFS ANGLEMIN ANGLEMAX' terms

r_clutter_distance.desc: Distance at which clutter will become invisible.

r_coronas.desc: Draw coronas on realtime lights. Overrides glquake-esque flashblends.

r_coronas_fadedist.desc: Coronas will fade out over this distance.

r_coronas_mindist.desc: Coronas closer than this will be invisible, preventing near clip plane issues.

r_coronas_occlusion.desc:
Specifies that coronas should be occluded more carefully.
0: No occlusion, at all.
1: BSP occlusion only (simple tracelines).
2: non-bsp occlusion also (complex tracelines).
3: Depthbuffer reads (forces synchronisation).
4: occlusion queries.

r_decal_noperpendicular.desc: When enabled, decals will not be generated on planes at a steep angle from clipped decal orientation.

r_deluxemapping.desc:
Enables bumpmapping based upon precomputed light directions.
0=off
1=use if available
2=auto-generate (if possible)

r_dimlight_colour.desc: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_DIMLIGHT effects (used for quad+pent in vanilla quake).

r_dodgymiptex.desc: When enabled, this will force regeneration of mipmaps, discarding mips1-4 like glquake did. This may eg solve fullbright issues with some maps, but may reduce distant detail levels.

r_dodgypcxfiles.desc: When enabled, this will ignore the palette stored within pcx files, for compatibility with quake2.

r_dodgytgafiles.desc: Many old glquake engines had a buggy tga loader that ignored bottom-up flags. Naturally people worked around this and the world was plagued with buggy images. Most engines have now fixed the bug, but you can reenable it if you have bugged tga files.

r_drawentities.desc:
Controls whether to draw entities or not.
0: Draw no entities.
1: Draw everything as normal.
2: Draw everything but bmodels.
3: Draw bmodels only.

r_drawflame.desc: Set to -1 to disable ALL static entities. Set to 0 to disable only wall torches and standing flame. Set to 1 for everything drawn as normal.

r_dynamic.desc: 0: no standard dlights at all.\n1: coloured dlights will be used, they may show through walls. These are not realtime things.\n2: The dlights will be forced to monochrome (this does not affect coronas/flashblends/rtlights attached to the same light).

r_editlights.desc: enables .rtlights file editing mode. Consider using csaddon/equivelent instead.

r_editlights_cursordistance.desc: maximum distance of cursor from eye

r_editlights_cursorgrid.desc: snaps cursor to this grid size

r_editlights_cursorpushback.desc: how far to pull the cursor back toward the eye, for some reason

r_editlights_cursorpushoff.desc: how far to push the cursor off the impacted surface

r_editlights_import_ambient.desc: ambient light scaler for imported lights

r_editlights_import_diffuse.desc: diffuse light scaler for imported lights

r_editlights_import_radius.desc: changes size of light entities loaded from a map

r_editlights_import_specular.desc: specular light scaler for imported lights

r_explosionlight_colour.desc: This controls the initial RGB values of EF_EXPLOSION effects.

r_explosionlight_fade.desc: This controls the per-second RGB decay values of EF_EXPLOSION effects.

r_fastturbcolour.desc: The colour to use for water surfaces draw with r_waterstyle 0.

r_fb_bmodels.desc: Enables loading lumas on the map, as well as any external bsp models.

r_fb_models.desc: Enables the use of lumas on models. Note that if ruleset_allow_fbmodels is enabled, then all models are unconditionally fullbright in deathmatch, because cheaters would set up their models like that anyway, hurrah for beating them at their own game. QuakeWorld players suck.

r_fog_cullentities.desc: 0: Never cull entities by fog...\n1: Automatically cull entities according to fog.\n2: Force fog culling regardless

r_fog_exp2.desc: Expresses how fog fades with distance. 0 (matching DarkPlaces's default) is typically more realistic, while 1 (matching FitzQuake and others) is more common.

r_fog_linear.desc: 0: Use Exp/Exp2 fog. 1: Use linear fog.

r_fog_permutation.desc: Renders fog using a material permutation. 0 plays nicer with q3 shaders, but 1 is otherwise a better choice.

r_font_postprocess_outline.desc: Controls the number of pixels of dark borders to use around fonts.

r_forceprogramify.desc: Reduce the shader to a single texture, and then make stuff up about its mother. The resulting fist fight results in more colour when you shine a light upon its face.\nSet to 2 to ignore 'depthfunc equal' and 'tcmod scale' in order to tolerate bizzare shaders made for a bizzare engine.\nBecause most shaders made for DP are by people who _clearly_ have no idea what the heck they're doing, you'll typically need the '2' setting.

r_fullbright.desc: Ignore world lightmaps, drawing *everything* fully lit.

r_fullbrightSkins.desc: Force the use of fullbright skins on other players. No more hiding in the dark.

r_fxaa.desc: Runs a post-procesing pass to strip the jaggies.

r_globalskin_count.desc: Specifies how many globalskins there are.

r_globalskin_first.desc: Specifies the first .skin value that is a global skin. Entities within this range will use the shader/image called 'gfx/skinSKIN.lmp' instead of their regular skin. See also: r_globalskin_count.

r_glsl_emissive.desc: When set, specifies that the _luma or _glow textures are emissive... When 0 they are taken as a mask for the proportion of the lightmap that will apply (for q2e compat, has issues with overbrights).

r_glsl_offsetmapping.desc: Enables the use of paralax mapping, adding fake depth to textures.

r_glsl_offsetmapping_reliefmapping.desc: Changes the paralax sampling mode to be a bit nicer, but noticably more expensive at high resolutions. r_glsl_offsetmapping must be set.

r_glsl_precache.desc: Force all relevant glsl permutations to load upfront.

r_glsl_skybox_autorotate.desc: Defines the axis around which skyboxes will rotate (the first three values). The fourth value defines the speed the skybox rotates at, in degrees per second.

r_glsl_skybox_orientation.desc: Defines the axis around which skyboxes will rotate (the first three values). The fourth value defines the speed the skybox rotates at, in degrees per second.

r_glsl_turbscale_reflect.desc: Controls the strength of the water reflection ripples (used by the altwater glsl code).

r_glsl_turbscale_refract.desc: Controls the strength of the underwater ripples (used by the altwater glsl code).

r_graphics.desc: Turning this off will result in ascii-style rendering.

r_greenlight_colour.desc: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_GREEN effects (rarely used).

r_halfrate.desc: Use half-rate shading (where supported by gpu).

r_hdr_framebuffer.desc: If enabled, the map will be rendered into a high-precision image framebuffer. This avoids issues with shaders that contribute more than 1 in any single pass (like overbrights). Can also be set to the name of an image format, to force rendering to that format first - interesting formats are L8, RGB565, B10G11R11F, and others.

r_ignoreentpvs.desc: Disables pvs culling of entities that have been submitted to the renderer.

r_ignoremapprefixes.desc: Ignores when textures were loaded from map-specific paths.\n0: textures/foo/tex.tga will not be confused with textures/foo/tex.tga.\n1: The same texture might be loaded multiple times over.

r_image_downloadsizelimit.desc: The maximum allowed file size of images loaded from a web-based url. 0 disables completely, while empty imposes no limit.

r_imageextensions.desc: The list of image file extensions which might exist on disk (note that this does not list all supported formats, only the extensions that should be searched for).

r_keepimages.desc: Retain unused images in memory for slightly faster map loading.\n0: Redundant images will be purged after each map change.\n1: Images will be retained until vid_reload (potentially consuming a lot of ram).

r_lavastyle.desc: See r_waterstyle, but affects only lava. If empty, defers to r_waterstyle.

r_lightmap_format.desc: Overrides the default texture format used for lightmaps. rgb9e5 is a good choice for HDR.

r_lightprepass.desc: Experimental. Attempt to use a different lighting mechanism (aka: deferred lighting). Requires vid_reload to take effect.

r_loadlit.desc:
Whether to load lit files.
0: Do not load external rgb lightmap data.
1: Load but don't generate.
2: Generate ldr lighting (if none found).
3: Generate hdr lighting (if none found).
Note that regeneration of lightmap data may be unreliable if the map was made for more advanced lighting tools.
Deluxemap information will also be generated, as appropriate.

r_loadsurfenvmaps.desc: Load local reflection environment-maps, where available. These are normally defined via env_cubemap entities dotted around the place.

r_lodbias.desc: Biases the level-of-detail on models (for those that have lod).

r_lodscale.desc: Scales the level-of-detail reduction on models (for those that have lod).

r_max_gpu_bones.desc: Specifies the maximum number of bones that can be handled on the GPU. If empty, will guess.

r_meshpitch.desc: Specifies the direction of the pitch angle on mesh models formats, Quake compatibility requires -1.

r_meshroll.desc: Specifies the direction of the roll angle on mesh models formats, also affects gamecode, so do not change from its default.

r_mirroralpha.desc: Specifies how the default shader is generated for the 'window02_1' texture. Values less than 1 will turn it into a mirror.

r_muzzleflash_colour.desc: This controls the initial RGB+radius of EF_MUZZLEFLASH/svc_muzzleflash effects.

r_muzzleflash_fade.desc: This controls the per-second RGB+radius decay of EF_MUZZLEFLASH/svc_muzzleflash effects.

r_netgraph.desc: Displays a graph of packet latency. A value of 2 will give additional info about what sort of data is being received from the server.

r_nolerp_list.desc: Models in this list will not interpolate. Any models included here should be considered bad.

r_noshadow_list.desc: Models in this list will not cast shadows.

r_part_classic_expgrav.desc: Scaler for how fast classic explosion particles should accelerate due to gravity. 1 for like vanilla, 10 for like zquake.

r_part_classic_opaque.desc: Disables transparency on classic particles, for the oldskool look.

r_part_classic_square.desc: Enables square particles, for the oldskool look.

r_part_contentswitch.desc: Enable particle effects to change based on content (ex. water).

r_part_rain.desc: Enable particle effects to emit off of surfaces. Mainly used for weather or lava/slime effects.

r_particle_tracelimit.desc: Number of traces to allow per frame for particle physics.

r_polygonoffset_submodel_factor.desc: z-fighting avoidance. Pushes submodel depth values slightly towards the camera depending on the slope of the surface.

r_polygonoffset_submodel_map.desc: List of maps on which z-fighting reduction should be used. wildcards accepted.

r_polygonoffset_submodel_offset.desc: z-fighting avoidance. Pushes submodel depth values slightly towards the camera by a consistent distance.

r_portaldrawplanes.desc: Draw front and back planes in portals. Debug feature.

r_portalonly.desc: Don't draw things which are not portals. Debug feature.

r_portalrecursion.desc: The number of portals the camera is allowed to recurse through.

r_postprocshader.desc: Specifies a custom shader to use as a post-processing shader

r_projection.desc:
0: regular perspective.
1: stereographic.
2: fisheye.
3: panoramic.
4: lambert azimuthal equal-area.
5: equirectangular.
6: panini.

r_redlight_colour.desc: The red, green, blue, radius values for EF_RED effects (typically used for pentagram in quakeworld).

r_refract_fbo.desc: Use an fbo for refraction. If 0, just renders as a portal and uses a copy of the current framebuffer.

r_refractreflect_scale.desc: Use a different scale for refraction and reflection texturemaps. Because $reasons.

r_renderscale.desc: Provides a way to enable subsampling or super-sampling

r_replacemodels.desc: A list of filename extensions to attempt to use instead of mdl.

r_rocketlight_colour.desc: This controls the RGB+radius values of MF_ROCKET effects.

r_shaderblobs.desc: If enabled, can massively accelerate vid restarts / loading (especially with the d3d renderer). Can cause issues when upgrading engine versions, so this is disabled by default.

r_shadow_bumpscale_basetexture.desc: bumpyness scaler for generation of fallback normalmap textures from models

r_shadow_heightscale_basetexture.desc: scaler for generation of height maps from legacy paletted content.

r_shadow_playershadows.desc: Controls the presence of shadows on the local player.

r_shadow_raytrace.desc: Enables use of hardware raytracing for shadows. Consider also using with r_halfrate.

r_shadow_realtime_dlight.desc: Enables the use of dynamic realtime lights, allowing explosions to use bumpmaps etc properly.

r_shadow_realtime_dlight_shadows.desc: Allows dynamic realtime lights to cast shadows as they move.

r_shadow_realtime_nonworld_lightmaps.desc: Scaler for lightmaps used when not using realtime world lighting. Probably broken.

r_shadow_realtime_world.desc: Enables the use of static/world realtime lights.

r_shadow_realtime_world_importlightentit.desc:
Controls default loading of map-based realtime lights.
0: Load explicit .rtlight files only.
1: Load explicit lights then try fallback to parsing the entities lump.
2: Load only the entities lump.

r_shadow_realtime_world_lightmaps.desc: Specifies how much of the map's normal lightmap to retain when using world realtime lights. 0 completely replaces lighting.

r_shadow_scissor.desc: constrains stencil shadows to the onscreen box that contains the maxmium extents of the light. This avoids unnecessary work.

r_shadow_shadowmapping.desc: Enables soft shadows instead of stencil shadows.

r_shadow_shadowmapping_precision.desc: Scales the shadowmap detail level up or down.

r_shadows.desc: Draw basic blob shadows underneath entities without using realtime lighting.

r_shadows_fakedistance.desc: The radius to use for fake shadows.

r_shadows_focus.desc: Offset for the center of the fake-shadows volume.

r_shadows_throwdirection.desc: The direction to throw the fake shadows in. Should ideally be opposite to r_sun_dir, but that just shows how fake these things actually are.

r_showbboxes.desc: Debugging. Shows bounding boxes. 1=ssqc, 2=csqc. Red=solid, Green=stepping/toss/bounce, Blue=onground.

r_showfields.desc: Debugging. Shows entity fields boxes (entity closest to crosshair). 1=ssqc, 2=csqc, 3=snapshots.

r_showshaders.desc: Debugging. Shows the name of the (worldmodel) shader being pointed to.

r_showtris.desc: Developer feature where everything is drawn with wireframe over the top. Only active where cheats are permitted.

r_skycloudalpha.desc: Controls how opaque the front layer of legacy scrolling skies should be.

r_skyfog.desc: This controls an alpha-blend value for fog on skyboxes, cumulative with regular fog alpha.

r_slimestyle.desc: See r_waterstyle, but affects only slime. If empty, defers to r_waterstyle.

r_softwarebanding.desc: Utilise the Quake colormap in order to emulate 8bit software rendering. This results in banding as well as other artifacts that some believe adds character. Also forces nearest sampling on affected surfaces (palette indicies do not interpolate well).

r_sprite_backfacing.desc: Make oriented sprites face backwards relative to their orientation, for compat with q1.

r_stereo_convergence.desc: Nudges the angle of each eye inwards when using stereoscopic rendering.

r_stereo_method.desc:
Value 0 = Off.
Value 1 = Attempt hardware acceleration. Requires vid_restart.
Value 2 = red/cyan.
Value 3 = red/blue.
Value 4=red/green.
Value 5=eye strain.

r_stereo_separation.desc: How far apart your eyes are, in quake units. A non-zero value will enable stereoscoping rendering. You might need some of them retro 3d glasses. Hardware support is recommended, see r_stereo_context.

r_sun_colour.desc: Specifies the colour of sunlight that appears in the form of crepuscular rays.

r_sun_dir.desc: Specifies the direction that crepusular rays appear along

r_telestyle.desc: See r_waterstyle, but affects only teleporters. If empty, defers to r_waterstyle.

r_temporalscenecache.desc: Controls whether to generate+reuse a scene cache over multiple frames. This is generated on a separate thread to avoid any associated costs. This can significantly boost framerates on complex maps, but can also stress the gpu more (performance tradeoff that varies per map). An outdated cache may be used if the cache takes too long to build (eg: lightmap animations), which could cause the odd glitch when moving fast (but retain more consistent framerates - another tradeoff).\n0: Tranditional quake rendering.\n1: Generate+Use the scene cache.

r_tessellation.desc: Enables+controls the use of blinn tessellation on the fallback shader for meshes, equivelent to a shader with 'program defaultskin#TESS'. This will look stupid unless the meshes were actually designed for it and have suitable vertex normals.

r_torch.desc: Generate a dynamic light at the player's position.

r_tracker_fadetime.desc: how long it takes for r_tracker messages to fully fade once they start fading\n

r_tracker_frags.desc:
0: like vanilla quake
1: shows only your kills/deaths
2: shows all kills

r_tracker_lines.desc: number of r_tracker messages to display\n

r_tracker_time.desc: how long it takes for r_tracker messages to start fading\n

r_tracker_w.desc: width of the r_tracker messages, as a fraction of the screen's width, eg 0.5\n

r_tracker_x.desc: left position of the r_tracker messages, as a fraction of the screen's width, eg 0.5\n

r_tracker_y.desc: top position of the r_tracker messages, as a fraction of the screen's height, eg 0.333\n

r_vertexdlights.desc: Determine model lighting with respect to nearby dlights. Poor-man's rtlights.

r_vertexlight.desc: Hack loaded shaders to remove detail pass and lightmap sampling for faster rendering.

r_viewmodel_fov.desc: field of vision, 1-170 degrees, standard fov is 90, nquake defaults to 108.

r_viewmodel_quake.desc: Controls whether to use weird viewmodel movements from vanilla quake.

r_viewpreselgun.desc: HACK: Display the preselected weaponmodel, instead of the current weaponmodel.

r_waterstyle.desc:
Changes how water, and teleporters are drawn. Possible values are:
0: fastturb-style block colour.
1: regular q1-style water.
2: refraction(ripply and transparent)
3: refraction with reflection at an angle
4: ripplemapped without reflections (requires particle effects)
5: ripples+reflections
