r_waterwarp.desc: Enables fullscreen warp, preferably via glsl. -1 specifies to force the fov warp fallback instead which can give a smidge more performance.

rank_autoadd.desc: Automatically register players into the ranking system

rank_filename.desc: Specifies which file to use as a rankings database. Enables the ranking system if set.

rank_needlogin.desc: If set to 1, prohibits players from joining if they're not yet registered. This will require an external mechanism to register users, presumably via rcon.

rank_parms_last.desc: Mod setting: the index of the last parm to be saved. Clamped to 32.

rate.desc: A rough measure of the bandwidth to try to use while playing. Too high a value may result in 'buffer bloat'.

record_flush.desc: If set, explicitly flushes demo data to disk while recording. This may be inefficient, depending on how your operating system is configured.

registered.desc: Set if quake's pak1.pak is available

ruleset.desc: Known rulesets are:\nnone: no explicit rules, all 'minor cheats' are allowed.\nstrict: equivelent to the smackdown ruleset. Note that this will block certain graphical enhancements too.

ruleset_allow_fbmodels.desc: When 1, allows all models to be displayed fullbright, completely ignoring the lightmaps. This feature exists only for parity with ezquake's defaults.

ruleset_allow_frj.desc: Specifies whether Forward-Rocket-Jump scripts are allowed in the current ruleset. If 0, limits on yaw speed will be imposed so they cannot be scripted.

ruleset_allow_larger_models.desc: Enforces a maximum bounds limit on models, to prevent the use of additional spikes attached to the model from being used as a kind of wallhack.

ruleset_allow_localvolume.desc: Allows the use of the snd_playersoundvolume cvar. Muting your own sounds can make it easier to hear where your opponent is.

ruleset_allow_modified_eyes.desc: When 0, completely hides progs/eyes.mdl if it is not strictly identical to vanilla quake.

ruleset_allow_overlong_sounds.desc: A setting of 0 will block the use of extra-long pickup sounds as item respawn timers.

ruleset_allow_packet.desc: If 0, network packets sent via the 'packet' command will be blocked. This makes scripting timers a little harder.

ruleset_allow_particle_lightning.desc: A setting of 0 blocks using the particle system to replace lightning gun trails. This prevents making the trails thinner thus preventing them from obscuring your view of your enemies.

ruleset_allow_playercount.desc: Specifies whether teamplay triggers that count nearby players are allowed in the current ruleset.

ruleset_allow_semicheats.desc: If 0, this blocks a range of cvars that are marked as semi-cheats. Such cvars will be locked to their empty/0 value.

ruleset_allow_sensitive_texture_replacem.desc: Allows the replacement of certain model textures (as well as the models themselves). This prevents adding extra fullbrights to make them blatently obvious.

ruleset_allow_shaders.desc: When 0, this completely disables the use of external shader files, preventing custom shaders from being used for wallhacks.

ruleset_allow_triggers.desc: When 0, blocks the use of msg_trigger checks.

ruleset_allow_watervis.desc: When 0, this enforces ugly opaque water.

s_al_debug.desc: Enables periodic checks for OpenAL errors.

s_al_disable.desc:
0: OpenAL works (generally as the highest priority).
1: OpenAL will be used only when a specific device is selected.
2: Don't allow ANY use of OpenAl.
With OpenAL disabled, audio ouput will fall back to platform-specific output, avoiding miscilaneous third-party openal limitation bugs.

s_al_distancemodel.desc:
Controls how sounds fade with distance.
0: Inverse (most realistic)
1: Inverse Clamped
2: Linear (Quake-like)
3: Linear Clamped
4: Exponential
5: Exponential Clamped
6: None

s_al_dopplerfactor.desc: Multiplies the strength of doppler effects.

s_al_hrtf.desc:
Enables use of HRTF, and which HRTF table to use.
empty: auto, depending on openal config to enable it.
\0: force off.
1: Use the default HRTF.

s_al_reference_distance.desc: This is the distance at which the sound is audiable with standard volume in the inverse distance models. Nearer sounds will be louder than the original sample.

s_al_speedofsound.desc: Configures the speed of sound, in game units per second. This affects doppler.

s_al_use_reverb.desc: Controls whether reverb effects will be used. Set to 0 to block them. Reverb requires gamecode to configure the reverb properties, other than underwater.

s_al_velocityscale.desc: Rescales velocity values, before doppler can be calculated.

s_ambientlevel.desc: This controls the volume levels of automatic area-based sounds (like water or sky), and is quite annoying. If you're playing deathmatch you'll definitely want this OFF.

s_device.desc: This is the sound device(s) to use, in the form of driver:device.\nIf desired, multiple devices can be listed in space-seperated (quoted) tokens. _s_device_opts contains any enumerated options.\nIn all seriousness, use the menu to set this if you wish to keep your hair.

s_doppler.desc: Enables doppler, with a multiplier for the scale.

s_doppler_max.desc: Highest allowed doppler scale, to avoid things getting too weird.

s_inactive.desc: Play sound while application is inactive (ie: tabbed out). Needs a snd_restart if changed.

s_khz.desc: Sound speed, in kilohertz. Common values are 11, 22, 44, 48. Values above 1000 are explicitly in hertz.

s_loadas8bit.desc: Downsample sounds on load as lower quality 8-bit sound, to save memory.

s_localvolume.desc: Sound level for sounds local or originating from the player such as firing and pain sounds.

s_mixahead.desc: Specifies how many seconds to prebuffer audio. Lower values give less latency, but might result in crackling. Different hardware/drivers have different tolerances, and this setting may be ignored completely where drivers are expected to provide their own tolerances.

s_mixerthread.desc: When enabled sound mixing will be run on a separate thread. Currently supported only by directsound. Other drivers may unconditionally thread audio. Set to 0 only if you have issues.

s_nominaldistance.desc: This cvar defines how far an attenuation=1 sound can be heard.

s_numspeakers.desc: Number of hardware audio channels to use.  supports up to 6.

sbar_teamstatus.desc: Display the last team say from each of your team members just above the sbar area.

scr_allowsnap.desc: Whether to allow server-requested screenshot requests to check for gpu driver hacks.

scr_autoid.desc: Display nametags above all players while spectating.

scr_autoid_armor.desc: Display armour as part of nametags (when known).

scr_autoid_enemycolour.desc: The colour for the text on the nametags of non-team members.

scr_autoid_health.desc: Display health as part of nametags (when known).

scr_autoid_team.desc: Display nametags above team members. 0: off. 1: display with half-alpha if occluded. 2: hide when occluded.

scr_autoid_teamcolour.desc: The colour for the text on the nametags of team members.

scr_autoid_weapon.desc: Display the player's best weapon as part of their nametag (when known).

scr_autoid_weapon_mask.desc:
Mask of bits for weapon icons to actually show.
+1: Shotgun.
+2: Super Shotgun.
+4: Nail Gun.
+8: Super Nail Gun.
+16: Grenade Launcher.
+32: Rocket Launcher.
+64: Lightning
Showing only RL and GL is 96

scr_centertime.desc: Centerprint messages will be displayed for this long before disappearing.

scr_conalpha.desc: How opaque the console should be when there's still stuff going on behind.

scr_consize.desc: Proportion of the screen to be covered by the console when its focused. Valid range is 0ish to 1.

scr_conspeed.desc: How fast the console careers onto the screen.

scr_fov_mode.desc:
Controls what the fov cvar actually controls:
0: largest axis (ultra-wide monitors means less height will be visible).
1: smallest axis (ultra-wide monitors will distort at the edges).
2: horizontal axis.
3: vertical axis.
4: 4:3 horizontal axis, padded for wider resolutions (for a more classic fov)

scr_loadingrefresh.desc: Force redrawing of the loading screen, in order to display EVERY resource that is loaded

scr_loadingscreen_aspect.desc:
Controls the aspect of levelshot images.
0: Use source image's aspect.
1: Force 4:3 aspect (ignore image's aspect), for best q3 compat.
2: Ignore aspect considerations and just smear it over the entire screen.
-1: Disable levelshot use.

scr_printspeed.desc: How rapidly each character is displayed during outro messages.

scr_scoreboard_afk.desc: Show 'afk' in the packetloss column when they're afk.

scr_scoreboard_backgroundalpha.desc: Further multiplier for the background alphas.

scr_scoreboard_drawtitle.desc: Wastes screen space when looking at the scoreboard.

scr_scoreboard_forcecolors.desc: Makes the scoreboard colours obey enemycolor/teamcolor rules.

scr_scoreboard_newstyle.desc: Display team colours and stuff in a style popularised by Electro. Looks more modern, but might not quite fit classic huds.

scr_scoreboard_ping_status.desc: Threshholds required to switch ping display from green to white, yellow, megenta and red.

scr_scoreboard_showflags.desc:
Display flag caps+touches on the scoreboard, where our fragfile.dat supports them.
0: off
1: on
2: on only if someone appears to have interacted with a flag.

scr_scoreboard_showfrags.desc: Display kills+deaths+teamkills, as determined by fragfile.dat-based conprint parsing. These may be inaccurate if you join mid-game.

scr_scoreboard_showhealth.desc:
Display health information when playing mvd/qtv streams.
0: off
1: on
2: show armour too. 3: combined health ('+' says more armour than health allows).

scr_scoreboard_showlocation.desc: Display player location names when playing mvd/qtv streams, if available.

scr_scoreboard_showweapon.desc: Display weapon information when playing mvd/qtv streams.

scr_scoreboard_teamsort.desc: On the scoreboard, sort players by their team BEFORE their personal score.

scr_sshot_compression.desc: Requsted compression ratio as a percentage. For jpeg this is the quantisation quality and has a direct impact on image quality vs size. For png this ranges between 0 for best and 100 for worst with final image quality being unchanged because png is loseless.

scr_sshot_type.desc: This specifies the default extension(and thus file format) for screenshots.\nKnown extensions are: png, jpg/jpeg, bmp, pcx, tga, ktx, dds.

scr_usekfont.desc: Exists for compat with the quake rerelease, changing the behaviour of QC's sprint/bprint/centerprint builtins.

show_fps.desc:
Displays the current framerate on-screen.
0: Off.
1: framerate average over a second.
2: Show a frametimes graph (with additional timing info).
-1: Normalized graph that focuses on the variation ignoring base times.

skyroom.desc: Specifies the center position of the skyroom's view. Skyrooms are drawn instead of skyboxes (typically with their own skybox around them). Entities in skyrooms will be drawn only when r_ignoreentpvs is 0. Can also be set with the _skyroom worldspawn key. This is overriden by csqc's VF_SKYROOM_CAMERA.

snd_ignorecueloops.desc: Ignores cue commands in wav files, for q3 compat.

snd_ignoregamespeed.desc: When set, allows sounds to desynchronise with game time or demo speeds.

snd_loadasstereo.desc: Force mono sounds to load as if stereo ones, to waste memory. Not normally useful.

snd_playbackrate.desc: Debugging cvar that changes the playback rate of all new sounds.

sv_aim.desc: The value should be cos(angle), where angle is the greatest allowed angle from which to deviate from the direction the shot would have been along. Values >1 thus disable auto-aim. This can be overridden with setinfo aim 0.73.

sv_antilag.desc:
Attempt to backdate impacts to compensate for lag via the MOVE_ANTILAG feature.
0=completely off.
1=mod-controlled (default).
2=forced, which might break certain uses of traceline.
3=Also attempt to recalculate trace start positions to avoid lagged knockbacks.

sv_autooffload.desc: Automatically start the server in a separate process, so that sporadic or persistent gamecode slowdowns do not affect visual framerates (equivelent to the mapcluster command). Note: Offloaded servers have separate cvar+command states which may complicate usage.

sv_autosave.desc: Interval for autosaves, in minutes. Set to 0 to disable autosave.

sv_banproxies.desc: If enabled, anyone connecting via known proxy software will be refused entry. This should aid with blocking aimbots, but is only reliable for certain public proxies.

sv_bigcoords.desc:
Uses floats for coordinates instead of 16bit values.
Also boosts angle precision, so can be useful even on small maps.
Affects clients thusly:
QW: enforces a mandatory protocol extension
DP: enables DPP7 protocol support
NQ: uses RMQ protocol (protocol 999).

sv_brokenmovetypes.desc: Emulate vanilla quakeworld by forcing MOVETYPE_WALK on all players. Shouldn't be used for any games other than QuakeWorld.

sv_calcphs.desc: Enables culling of sound effects. 0=always skip phs. Sounds are globally broadcast. 1=always generate phs. Sounds are always culled. On large maps the phs will be dumped to disk. 2=On large single-player maps, generation of phs is skipped. Otherwise like option 1.

sv_crypt_rcon.desc:
Controls whether the rcon password must be hashed or not. Hashed passwords also partially prevent replay attacks, but does NOT prevent malicious actors from reading the commands/results.
0: completely insecure. ONLY allows plain-text passwords. Do not use.
1: Mandatory hashing (recommended).
Empty: Allow either, whether the password is secure or not is purely the client's responsibility/fault. Only use this for comptibility with old clients.

sv_csqcdebug.desc: Inject packet size information for data directed to csqc.

sv_cullentities_trace.desc: Attempt to cull non-player entities using tracelines as an extreeme anti-wallhack.

sv_cullplayers_trace.desc: Attempt to cull player entities using tracelines as an anti-wallhack.

sv_demoAutoCompress.desc: Specifies whether to compress demos as they're recorded.\n0 = no compression.\n1 = gzip compression.

sv_demoAutoRecord.desc: If set, automatically record demos.\n-1: record on client connection only.\n1+: record once there's this many active players on the server (or if connected to a remote server).

sv_demoClearOld.desc: Automatically delete demos to keep the demos count reasonable.

sv_demoDirAlt.desc: Provides a fallback directory name for demo downloads, for when sv_demoDir doesn't contain the requested demo.

sv_demoExtensions.desc:
Enables protocol extensions within MVDs. This will cause older/non-fte clients to error upon playback.
0: off.
1: all extensions.
2: extensions also supported by a certain other engine.

sv_demoMaxDirAge.desc: Maximum allowed age for demos, any older demos will be deleted when sv_demoClearOld is set (this doesn't prevent recording new demos).

sv_demoMaxDirCount.desc: Maximum allowed serverside mvds to record. Set to 0 to remove the limit. New demos cannot be recorded once this many demos have already been recorded.

sv_demoMaxDirSize.desc: Maximum allowed serverside storage space for mvds. set to blank to remove the limit. New demos cannot be recorded once this size is reached.

sv_demoMaxSize.desc: Demos will be truncated to be no larger than this size.

sv_demoPings.desc: Interval between ping updates in mvds

sv_demoUseCache.desc: If set, demo data will be flushed only periodically

sv_demo_write_csqc.desc: Writes a copy of the csprogs into recorded demos. This ensures that the demo can be played back despite future gamecode changes.

sv_dlURL.desc: Provides clients with an external url from which they can obtain pk3s/packages from an external http server instead of having to download over udp.

sv_ftp_port_range.desc: Specifies the port range for the server to create listening sockets for 'active' ftp connections, to work around NAT/firewall issues.\nMost FTP clients should use passive connections, but there's still some holdouts like windows.

sv_fulllevel.desc: User accounts with an access level greater than this may write anywhere, including the gamedir. Note that setting this low is increadibly risky. An empty value will be understood to never give this permission.

sv_fullredirect.desc: This is the ip:port to redirect players to when the server is full

sv_gameplayfix_blowupfallenzombies.desc: Allow findradius to find non-solid entities. This may break certain mods. It is better for mods to use FL_FINDABLE_NONSOLID instead.

sv_gameplayfix_droptofloorstartsolid.desc: When droptofloor fails, this causes a second attemp, but with traceline instead.

sv_gameplayfix_findradiusdistancetobox.desc: When 1, findradius checks to the nearest part of the entity instead of only its origin, making it find slightly more entities.

sv_gameplayfix_grenadebouncedownslopes.desc: MOVETYPE_BOUNCE speeds are calculated relative to the impacted surface, instead of the vertical, reducing the chance of grenades just sitting there on slopes.

sv_gameplayfix_multiplethinks.desc: Enables multiple thinks per entity per frame so small nextthink times are accurate. QuakeWorld mods expect a value of 1, while NQ expects 0.

sv_gameplayfix_nolinknonsolid.desc: When 0, setorigin et al will not link the entity into the collision nodes (which is faster, especially if you have a lot of non-solid entities. When 1, allows entities to freely switch between .solid values (except for SOLID_BSP) without relinking. A lot of DP mods assume a value of 1 and will bug out otherwise, while 0 will restore a bugs present in various mods.

sv_gameplayfix_setmodelrealbox.desc: Vanilla setmodel will setsize the entity to a hardcoded size for non-bsp models. This cvar will always use the real size of the model instead, but will require that the server actually loads the model.

sv_gameplayfix_setmodelsize_qw.desc: The setmodel builtin will act as a setsize for QuakeWorld mods also.

sv_gameplayfix_spawnbeforethinks.desc: Fixes an issue where player thinks (including Pre+Post) can be called before PutClientInServer. Unfortunately at least one mod depends upon PreThink being called first in order to correctly determine spawn positions.

sv_gameplayfix_stepdown.desc: Attempt to step down steps, instead of only up them. Affects non-predicted movetype_walk.

sv_gameplayfix_trappedwithin.desc: Blocks further entity movement when an entity is already inside another entity. This ensures that bsp precision issues cannot allow the entity to completely pass through eg the world.

sv_getrealip.desc:
Attempt to obtain a more reliable IP for clients, rather than just their proxy.
0: Don't attempt.
1: Unreliable checks.
2: Validate if possible.
3: Mandatory validation.

sv_guidkey.desc: If set, clients will calculate their GUID values against this string instead of the server's IP address. This allows consistency between multiple servers (for stats tracking), but do NOT treat the client's GUID as something that is secure.

sv_heartbeat_checks.desc: Report when sv_public 1 fails due to PROBABLE router/NAT issues.

sv_heartbeat_interval.desc: Interval between heartbeats. Low values are abusive, high values may cause NAT/ghost issues.

sv_limittics.desc: The maximum number of ticks that may be run within a frame, to allow the server to catch up if it stalled or if sv_maxtic is too low.

sv_listen_dp.desc: Allows the server to respond with the DP-specific handshake protocol.\nWarning: this can potentially get confused with quake2, and results in race conditions with both vanilla netquake and quakeworld protocols.\nOn the plus side, DP clients can usually be identified correctly, enabling a model+sound limit boost.

sv_listen_nq.desc:
Allow new (net)quake clients to connect to the server.
0 = don't let them in.
1 = allow them in (WARNING: this allows 'qsmurf' DOS attacks).
2 = accept (net)quake clients by emulating a challenge (as secure as QW/Q2 but does not fully conform to the NQ protocol).
You may also need to set net_enable_dtls if you wish for the rerelease's client to connect.

sv_listen_qw.desc: Specifies whether normal clients are allowed to connect.

sv_maxaim.desc: The maximum acceptable angle for autoaiming.

sv_maxdrate.desc: This cvar controls the maximum number of bytes sent to each player per second while that player is downloading.\nIf this cvar is set to 0, there will be NO CAP for download rates (if the user's drate is empty/0 too, then expect really fast+abusive downloads that could potentially be considered denial of service attacks)

sv_maxrate.desc: This controls the maximum number of bytes any indivual player may receive (when not downloading). The individual user's rate will also be controlled by the user's rate cvar.

sv_maxtic.desc: The maximum interval between running physics frames. If the value is too low, multiple physics interations might be run at a time (based upon sv_limittics). Set to 0 for fixed-interval ticks, which may be required if ODE is used.

sv_minping.desc: Simulate fake lag for any players with a ping under the value specified here. Value is in milliseconds.

sv_mintic.desc: The minimum interval between running physics frames.

sv_nailhack.desc: If set to 1, disables the nail entity networking optimisation. This hack was popularised by qizmo which recommends it for better compression. Also allows clients to interplate nail positions and add trails.

sv_nopvs.desc: Set to 1 to ignore pvs on the server. This can make wallhacks more dangerous, so should only be used for debugging.

sv_nqplayerphysics.desc: Disable player prediction and run NQ-style player physics instead. This can be used for compatibility with mods that expect exact behaviour. A value of 2 will not block prediction, and may be juddery/jerky/swimmy.

sv_phs.desc: If 1, do not use the phs. It is generally better to use sv_calcphs instead, and leave this as 1.

sv_ping_ignorepl.desc: If 1, ping times reported for players will ignore the effects of packetloss on ping times. 0 is slightly more honest, but less useful for connection diagnosis.

sv_playerslots.desc: Specify maximum number of player/spectator/bot slots, new value takes effect on the next map (this may result in players getting kicked). This should generally be set to maxclients+maxspectators. Leave blank for a default value.\nMaximum value of . Values above 16 will result in issues with vanilla NQ clients. Effective values other than 32 will result in issues with vanilla QW clients.

sv_port.desc: Port number to list on for inbound udp-based connections (including dtls variants). Can be a list for multiple ports. If ips are included then binds to that specific interface. Whether any specific protocol is accepted depends upon other settings.

sv_port_ipv6.desc: Port to use for incoming ipv6 udp connections. Due to hybrid sockets this might not be needed. You can specify an ipv4 address:port for a second ipv4 port if you want.

sv_port_natpmp.desc: If set (typically to 5351), automatically configures your router's port forwarding. You can instead specify the full ip address of your router (192.168.1.1:5351 for example). Your router must have NAT-PMP supported and enabled.

sv_port_rtc.desc: This specifies the broker url to use to obtain clients from. If the hostname is ommitted, it'll come from the manifest. If omitted, the broker service will randomize the resource part, so be sure to tell your friends the path reported by eg status rather than just this cvar value. Or just set it to 'rtc:///example' and tell clients to connect to the same sservevalue.

sv_port_tcp.desc: Port number to list on for inbound tcp-based connections (including tls variants). Can be a list for multiple ports. If ips are included then binds to that specific interface. Whether any specific protocol is accepted depends upon other settings.

sv_port_tcp6.desc: Equivelent to sv_port_tcp, but port numbers are assumed to be ipv6 only. relevant only when not using hybrid sockets.

sv_progs.desc: Specifies the filename of the gamecode to use serverside. Empty means autodetect - typically loading either progs or qwprogs depending on gamedir priority, then based upon deathmatch settings.

sv_protocol.desc: Specifies which protocol extensions to force. Clients which do not support the named protocols will be kicked. Recognised values: fte1 fte2 csqc.

sv_protocol_nq.desc:
Specifies the default protocol to use for new NQ clients. This is only relevent for clients that do not report their supported protocols. Supported values are
0 = autodetect
15 = vanilla
666 = fitzquake
999 = rmq protocol
The sv_bigcoords cvar forces upgrades as required.

sv_public.desc:
-1: Fully blocks all inbound connections.
0: Disable subscribing to master servers (for private lan-only games).
1: Subscribe to public master servers. Your IP address will be listed publicly. Make sure your Router/NAT+Firewall are set to allow inbound connections.
2: Subscribe to a broker master, allowing firewall hole punching.

sv_pupglow.desc: Instructs clients to enable hexen2-style powerup pulsing.

sv_pure.desc:
The most evil cvar in the world, many clients will ignore this.
0=standard quake rules.
1=clients should prefer files within packages present on the server.
2=clients should use *only* files within packages present on the server.
Due to quake 1.01/1.06 differences, a setting of 2 only works in total conversions.

sv_realip_kick.desc: Kicks clients if their realip could not be validated to the level specified by sv_getrealip.

sv_realiphostname_ipv4.desc: This is the server's public ip:port. This is needed for realip to work when the autodetected/local ip is not globally routable

sv_realiphostname_ipv6.desc: This is the server's public ip:port. This is needed for realip to work when the autodetected/local ip is not globally routable

sv_reconnectlimit.desc: Blocks dupe connection within the specified length of time .

sv_reliable_sound.desc: Causes all sounds to be sent reliably, so they will not be missed due to packetloss. However, this will cause them to be delayed somewhat, and slightly bursty. This can be overriden using the 'rsnd' userinfo setting (either forced on or forced off). Note: this does not affect sounds attached to particle effects.

sv_reportheartbeats.desc: Print a notice each time a heartbeat is sent to a master server. When set to 2, the message will be displayed once.

sv_savefmt.desc:
Specifies the format used for the saved game.
0=legacy.
1=fte
2=binary

sv_serverip.desc: Set this cvar to the server's public ip address if the server is behind a firewall and cannot detect its own public address. Providing a port is required if the firewall/nat remaps it, but is otherwise optional.

sv_showconnectionlessmessages.desc: Display a line describing each connectionless message that arrives on the server. Primarily a debugging feature, but also potentially useful to admins.

sv_showpredloss.desc: Print messages whenever input frames are ignored or forced serverside, to prevent speedcheats or hover cheats. Any such prints will be accompanied by prediction misses in the named client.

sv_specprint.desc:
Bitfield that controls which player events spectators see when tracking that player.
&1: spectators will see centerprints.
&2: spectators will see sprints (pickup messages etc).
&4: spectators will receive console commands, this is potentially risky.
Individual spectators can use 'setinfo sp foo' to limit this setting.

sv_timestamplen.desc: Limits clock skew to reduce (delayed) replay attacks

sv_use_dns.desc: Performs a reverse-dns lookup in order to report more info about where clients are connecting from.

sv_userinfo_bytelimit.desc: This is the maximum number of bytes that may be stored into each user's userinfo. Note that this includes key names too.

sv_userinfo_keylimit.desc: This is the maximum number of userinfo keys each user may create.

sv_voip_echo.desc: Echo voice packets back to their sender, a debug/test setting.

sv_voip_record.desc: Record voicechat into mvds. Requires player support. 0=noone, 1=everyone, 2=spectators only

sv_wallfriction.desc: Additional friction when running into walls

sv_writelevel.desc: Specifies the required trust level at which user accounts may write to the user-specific subdir of /uploads/USERNAME/*. If blank, then no uploads are permitted

sys_clockprecision.desc: Attempts to control windows' interrupt interval, in milliseconds. This can cause windows to give better clock precision and shorter waits, but also more overhead from process rescheduling.

sys_clocktype.desc:
Controls which system clock to base timings from.
0: auto
1: gettimeofday (may be discontinuous).
2: monotonic.

sys_colorconsole.desc: Parse colour escapes, with ansi colours on stdout.

sys_keepscreenon.desc: If set, the screen will never darken. This might cost some extra battery power, but then so will running a 3d engine.

sys_orientation.desc: Specifies what angle to render quake at.\nValid values are: sensor (autodetect), landscape, portrait, reverselandscape, reverseportrait

timeout.desc: Connections will time out if no packets are received for this duration of time.

tls_ignorecertificateerrors.desc: This should NEVER be set to 1!

tls_provider.desc: Controls which TLS provider to use.

tts_mode.desc:
Text to speech
0: off
1: Read only chat messages with a leading 'tts ' prefix.
2: Read all chat messages
3: Read every single console print.

utf8_enable.desc: When 1, changes the qc builtins to act upon codepoints instead of bytes. Do not use unless com_parseutf8 is also set.

v_bonusflash.desc: Controls the strength of temporary screen flashes when picking up items (gl_polyblend must be enabled).

v_contentblend.desc: Controls the strength of underwater colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).

v_cshift_empty.desc: The colour tint to use when in the open air (additionally scaled by v_contentblend.

v_cshift_lava.desc: The colour tint to use when burried in lava (ouchie!) (additionally scaled by v_contentblend.

v_cshift_slime.desc: The colour tint to use when submerged in slime (additionally scaled by v_contentblend.

v_cshift_water.desc: The colour tint to use when underwater (additionally scaled by v_contentblend.

v_damagecshift.desc: Controls the strength of damage-taken colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).

v_deathtilt.desc: Specifies whether to tilt the view when dead.

v_depthsortentities.desc: Reorder entities for transparency such that the furthest entities are drawn first, allowing nearer transparent entities to draw over the top of them.

v_gammainverted.desc: Boolean that controls whether the gamma should be inverted (like quake) or not.

v_gunkick.desc: Controls the strength of view angle changes when firing weapons.

v_gunkick_q2.desc: Controls the strength of view angle changes when firing weapons (in Quake2).

v_idlescale.desc: Enable swishing of the view (whether idle or otherwise). Often used for concussion effects.

v_kickpitch.desc: This controls part of the strength of viewangle changes from taking damage.

v_kickroll.desc: This controls part of the strength of viewangle changes from taking damage.

v_kicktime.desc: This controls how long viewangle changes from taking damage will last.

v_pentcshift.desc: Controls the strength of pentagram-of-protection colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).

v_quadcshift.desc: Controls the strength of quad-damage colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).

v_ringcshift.desc: Controls the strength of ring-of-invisibility colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).

v_suitcshift.desc: Controls the strength of envirosuit colour tints (gl_polyblend must be enabled).

vid_baseheight.desc: Specifies a mod's target height and used only when the 2d scale is not otherwise forced. Unlike vid_conheight the size is not fixed and will be padded to avoid inconsistent filtering.

vid_bpp.desc: The number of colour bits to request from the renedering context

vid_conautoscale.desc: Changes the 2d scale, including hud, console, and fonts. To specify an explicit font size, divide the desired 'point' size by 8 to get the scale. High values will be clamped to maintain at least a 320*200 virtual size.

vid_conheight.desc: Specifies the virtual height of the screen. If 0, will be inferred by vid_conwidth or other settings, according to aspect etc.

vid_conwidth.desc: Specifies the virtual width of the screen. Should generally be left as 0 to allow the correct aspect to be used despite video mode changes.

vid_depthbits.desc: The number of depth bits to request from the renedering context. Try 24.

vid_desktopgamma.desc: Apply gamma ramps upon the desktop rather than the window.

vid_desktopsettings.desc: Ignore the values of vid_width and vid_height, and just use the same settings that are used for the desktop.

vid_devicename.desc: Specifies which video device to try to use. If blank or invalid then one will be guessed.

vid_dpi_x.desc: For mods that need to determine the physical screen size (like with touchscreens). 0 means unknown

vid_dpi_y.desc: For mods that need to determine the physical screen size (like with touchscreens). 0 means unknown

vid_fullscreen.desc:
Specifies whether the game should be fullscreen or not (requires vid_restart).
0: Run in a resizable window, which can be manually maximized (with borders).
1: Traditional fullscreen-exclusive video mode with mode switching and everything.
2: Simply maximize the window and hide any borders without interfering with any other parts of the system.

vid_gl_context_compatibility.desc: Requests an OpenGL context with fixed-function backwards compat.

vid_gl_context_debug.desc: Requests a debug opengl context. This provides better error oreporting.

vid_gl_context_es.desc: Requests an OpenGLES context. Be sure to set vid_gl_context_version to 2 or so.

vid_gl_context_forwardcompatible.desc: Requests an opengl context with no depricated features enabled.

vid_gl_context_noerror.desc: Disables OpenGL's error checks for a small performance speedup. May cause segfaults if stuff wasn't properly implemented/tested.

vid_gl_context_robustness.desc: Attempt to enforce extra buffer protection in the gl driver, but can be slower with pre-gl3 hardware.

vid_gl_context_selfreset.desc: Upon hardware failure, have the engine create a new context instead of depending on the drivers to restore everything. This can help to avoid graphics drivers randomly killing your game, and can help reduce memory requirements.

vid_gl_context_version.desc: Specifies the version of OpenGL to try to create.

vid_hardwaregamma.desc: Use hardware gamma ramps. 0=ugly texture-based gamma, 1=glsl(windowed) or hardware(fullscreen), 2=always glsl, 3=always hardware gamma (disabled if hardware doesn't support), 4=scene-only gamma.

vid_height.desc: The screen height to attempt to use, in physical pixels. 0 means use desktop resolution.

vid_minsize.desc: Specifies a mod's minimum virtual size (to be set inside the mod's default.cfg file). The virtual size will always be at least this big. Windows may not be resized below this value either (which may reduce video mode options), but might require a vid_restart to take effect when switching between mods.

vid_multisample.desc: The number of samples to use for Multisample AntiAliasing (aka: msaa). A value of 1 explicitly disables it.

vid_preservegamma.desc: Restore initial hardware gamma ramps when quitting.

vid_renderer.desc: Specifies which backend is used. Values that might work are: sv (dedicated server), headless (null renderer), vk (vulkan), gl (opengl), egl (opengl es), d3d9 (direct3d 9), d3d11 (direct3d 11, with default hardware rendering), d3d11 warp (direct3d 11, with software rendering).

vid_srgb.desc:
-1: Only the framebuffer should use sRGB colourspace, textures and colours will be assumed to be linear. This has the effect of just brightening the screen according to a gamma ramp of about 2.2 (or .45 in quake's backwards gamma terms).
0: Off. Colour blending will be wrong, you're likely to see obvious banding.
1: Use sRGB extensions/support to ensure that the lighting aproximately matches real-world lighting (required for PBR).
2: Attempt to use a linear floating-point framebuffer, which should enable monitor support for HDR.
Note that driver behaviour varies by a disturbing amount, and much of the documentation conflicts with itself (the term 'linear' is awkward when the eye's perception of linear is non-linear).

vid_triplebuffer.desc: Specifies whether the hardware is forcing tripplebuffering on us, this is the number of extra page swaps required before old data has been completely overwritten.

vid_width.desc: The screen width to attempt to use, in physical pixels. 0 means use desktop resolution.

vid_winthread.desc: When enabled, window messages will be handled by a separate thread. This allows the game to continue rendering when Microsoft Windows blocks while resizing, etc.

vid_wndalpha.desc: When running windowed, specifies the window's transparency level.

vk_amd_rasterization_order.desc: Enables the use of relaxed rasterization ordering, for a small speedup at the minor risk of a little zfighting.

vk_busywait.desc: Force busy waiting until the GPU finishes doing its thing.

vk_debug.desc: Register a debug handler to display driver/layer messages. 2 enables the standard validation layers.

vk_dualqueue.desc: Attempt to use a separate queue for presentation. Blank for default.

vk_khr_dedicated_allocation.desc: Flag vulkan memory allocations as dedicated, where applicable.

vk_stagingbuffers.desc: Configures which dynamic buffers are copied into gpu memory for rendering, instead of reading from shared memory. Empty for default settings.\nAccepted chars are u(niform), e(lements), v(ertex), 0(none).

vk_submissionthread.desc: Execute submits+presents on a thread dedicated to executing them. This may be a significant speedup on certain drivers.

vk_usememorypools.desc: Allocates memory pools for sub allocations. Vulkan has a limit to the number of memory allocations allowed so this should always be enabled, however at this time FTE is unable to reclaim pool memory, and would require periodic vid_restarts to flush them.

vk_waitfence.desc: Waits on fences, instead of semaphores. This is more likely to result in gpu stalls while the cpu waits.

volume.desc: Volume level for game sounds (does not affect music, voice, or cinematics).

votelevel.desc: This is the restriction level of commands that players may vote for. You can reconfigure commands, cvars, or aliases individually. Additionally, aliases can be configured via aliaslevel to be executed at a different level from their restriction level. This can be used to indirectly allow voting for 'map dm4' for instance, without allowing people to vote for every map.

voteminimum.desc: At least this many players must vote the same way for the vote to pass.

votepercent.desc: At least this percentage of players must vote the same way for the vote to pass.

votetime.desc: Votes will be discarded after this many minutes

wasapi_exclusive.desc: When set, attempts to take exclusive control of the output device, to the detriment of other programs (causing errors or even crashes in them).\nExclusive mode leaves the game free to change the hardware's playback details, instead of being required to use a single system-wide 'mixer' rate.\nIt should also reduce latency a little.

wasapi_forcechannels.desc: Attempts to force snd_numchannels instead of using the system's default channel count.\nFor this to work, you will need to set wasapi_exclusive 1

wasapi_forcerate.desc: Attempts to force snd_khz instead of using the system's default channel count.\nFor this to work, you will need to set wasapi_exclusive 1

worker_count.desc: Specifies the number of worker threads to utilise.

worker_flush.desc: If set, process the entire load queue, loading stuff faster but at the risk of stalling the main thread.

worker_sleeptime.desc: Causes workers to sleep for a period of time after each job.

zombietime.desc: Client slots will not be reused for this number of seconds.
